# Development Progress & Stage Roadmap

**Project**: Telegram Mini App for managing interior finishing and renovation work in Poland.  
**Repository**: `git@github.com:kukhmax/plan_-_estimate.git`  
**Central Entity**: OBIEKT (Project / Site)  
**Stack**: React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind CSS | Python + FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2.x + Alembic + Pydantic v2 + PostgreSQL | aiogram 3.x

> **Document purpose.** `docs/development-progress.md` is the canonical progress **INDEX**. It answers quickly: what
> stages exist, what is complete, what is in progress, what comes next, and where the detailed documentation lives.
> Detailed architecture and implementation decisions remain in their stage-specific documents (listed in the roadmap
> table below). The long per-stage history further down (archived overview detail, historical mapping, Stage Log) is
> preserved as a record and is not a specification.
>
> **Last index update**: 2026-10-08 (**Stage 14 COMPLETE / OWNER ACCEPTED** (14A–14K); earlier note: **14E photo UI deployed**: production runs

  - **Accepted implementation**:
    - `PhotoUploadService` (`app/domain/services/photo_upload_service.py`): domain orchestration after bounded
      reception (`PhotoUploadRequest` / `PhotoUploadResult` / `PhotoUploadOutcome` / `PhotoUploadConfig`); upload gate
      first; additive `ImageProcessor.slot()` / `run_in_slot()` and `validate_attachment_fields`; upload exceptions
      `PHOTO_UPLOADS_DISABLED`, `PHOTO_UPLOAD_MALFORMED`, `PHOTO_UPLOAD_ID_CONFLICT`, `PHOTO_STORAGE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`,
      `PHOTO_UPLOAD_RESUME_MISMATCH`; storage failures stay provider-neutral `MediaStorageError` subclasses.
    - Logical photo quota accounting (`app/domain/services/photo_quota.py`): READY + PENDING + FAILED, archived
      included, recorded sizes only, no bucket scan; OK / WARNING / FULL; soft cap for new uploads only.
    - Canonical lowercase UUIDv4 `upload_id`; uniform `upload_id` conflict semantics (one identical error for a
      foreign id, an own id of another project and an own id with different bytes); ownership/project validation
      before any SHA comparison.
    - New upload: processing → quota → atomic PENDING asset + first attachment → write-once original / display /
      thumbnail → CAS READY.
    - READY replay, including archived assets.
    - PENDING / FAILED resume: FAILED → PENDING CAS recovery claim; per-object HEAD / resume; retry SHA-256
      verification before any original re-PUT; derivative reproduction checks (format / dimensions / sizes); no
      ETag-as-SHA assumption.
    - Replay and resume bypass the NEW-upload quota rejection; request metadata ignored during replay/resume; no
      duplicate first attachment; no object deletion; storage/object failures remain detectable by the integrity
      tooling (`PENDING_INCOMPLETE` / `FAILED_RELATED`, never `ORPHAN_CANDIDATE`); READY cannot regress.
  - **Owner concurrency review (PASS)**:
    - The arbitrary 4-round retry/livelock guard was **removed**; state-machine / CAS convergence is used instead, and
      CAS losers re-read the current state.
    - Concurrent PENDING resumes are safe through immutable / write-once storage + CAS; concurrent FAILED resumes use
      FAILED → PENDING CAS as the claim.
    - Stale failure handling cannot regress READY; a storage failure racing with a successful READY preserves READY.
    - A FAILED-state commit failure may leave a `PENDING_INCOMPLETE` row that is recoverable on retry.
    - The original first attachment and its metadata remain stable.

- **Drift discovered**: the owner's 14C.7B production build of `7bba6c8` (image

  only ranges, Starlette / anyio / botocore were not declared at all, and there was no lock or constraints file, so
  every uncached build re-resolved. The plan's STOP condition (FastAPI / Starlette / python-multipart minor bump) held;
  the drifted image `d9e5937…` was **never deployed** (no container was recreated).

  `~/backups/plan-estimate/backend-pre-14c7-pip-freeze.txt`, SHA256

  (since the Stage 13E.5B greenlet fix), Starlette 1.7.0, Uvicorn 0.54.0, Alembic 1.20.0 and PyJWT 2.15.0 — newer
  than the local Python 3.14 14C.6 venv (2.0.52 / 1.6.0 / 0.52.4 / 1.19.2 / 2.13.0).
- **Decision (owner)**: do not downgrade production to the local 14C.6 venv. Pre-14C dependencies keep the versions
  already proven by the running production runtime; the dependency new in 14C (python-multipart 0.0.32) keeps the
  14C.6-accepted version; the Stage 14C code is re-verified on that set under Python 3.12.

  tools installed in the image, and explicit pins for transitive packages the app imports directly or that define the
  runtime contract: Starlette, anyio, greenlet, botocore, s3transfer, urllib3, h11, httptools, uvloop).
  `pyproject.toml` unchanged (Docker installs `requirements.txt` only). New guard

  are present, installed versions equal the pins (PEP 503 name normalization, extras parsed), and pinned extras are
  installed; `requirements.txt` is the only version source. Inside a built image it rejects a drifted build.
- **Starlette 1.6 → 1.7 parser exception normalization (owner-approved test change)**: the first local run on the
  pinned set had one failure, the 14C.4 characterisation test
  `test_non_multipart_body_raises_a_raw_python_multipart_error`, which asserted a Starlette 1.6.0 internal (a raw
  python-multipart `FormParserError` escaping the parser). Starlette 1.7.0 — already running in production — wraps it
  in `MultiPartException`, which `Request.form` turns into a 400 that the route remaps to 422. The public behaviour was
  unchanged (`test_malformed_multipart_is_422[garbage]`: 422 `PHOTO_UPLOAD_MALFORMED`). With the owner's approval the
  test was replaced (not deleted) by `test_any_framework_multipart_failure_is_normalized_to_422`, which tests the
  application normalization boundary instead of framework internals: it injects each framework failure shape at the
  parser (raw `FormParserError`, raw `MultipartParseError`, Starlette `MultiPartException`; Starlette's own
  conversion in `Request.form` still runs) and asserts 422, the exact `PHOTO_UPLOAD_MALFORMED` detail, no DB rows,
  clean temp and released admission. It adds coverage: on Starlette 1.7.0 no real body reaches the route's
  `except FormParserError` branch, so the existing API cases could not detect its removal; in a scratch copy (repository
  untouched) removing that branch fails the two raw cases and removing the 400 remap fails the Starlette case.

### Stage 14D.1 — media backup / restore architecture & readiness audit (2026-10-02, OWNER APPROVED)

Documentation only (no code, migration, requirement, cloud resource, credential, SSH or production action).
Canonical contract: `docs/STAGE_14D_BACKUP_RESTORE_PLAN.md`.

- **Audit findings**: no backup / manifest / restore tooling; **DB dumps exist only on the production VM**; no
  derivative-regeneration tool (derivative bytes are not guaranteed reproducible and the DB stores no derivative
  hash); Oracle write-once / overwrite / ETag behaviour through the S3 adapter unverified; single-store
  configuration; no read-only R2 token, no Oracle identity, no drill buckets; runbook §72 still a draft.
- **Owner decisions**: R2 stays primary; Oracle Object Storage is the independent backup provider; same immutable
  keys; manifest v1 + `COMPLETE.json`; database-driven backup; **all three objects of every READY asset are backed
  up** (derivatives not regenerable in v1); Frankfurt EU region if supported; provisional buckets
  `plan-estimate-media-backup`, `plan-estimate-media-drill-backup` (Oracle) and `plan-estimate-media-drill-source`,
  `plan-estimate-media-drill-restore` (R2) as operational configuration only; separate least-privilege backup and
  restore credentials, exact Oracle IAM semantics verified empirically in 14D.3 / 14D.4; DB dumps **encrypted with
  `age` before leaving the VM** (decryption key never only on the VM; nothing secret in Git); drill restore target is
  a separate R2 bucket (never a prefix in the production bucket); drill preferably on the Oracle VM with isolated
  scratch containers / databases (production PostgreSQL never a restore target); retention v1 append-only, no
  automatic deletion, no irreversible lock; recurring backups eventually via a dedicated read-only PostgreSQL role
  (manual operational step, not a migration); no timer in 14D.1 / 14D.2; sub-stages 14D.2–14D.7 approved.

  (`pg_export_snapshot()` + `pg_dump --snapshot`) with `ready_count` / `ready_set_sha256`, and `COMPLETE.json` is
  written only if every READY asset of that snapshot is represented by all three verified objects (independently
  re-checkable from the restored dump); (B) an existing target object is admitted only with a SHA-256 recomputed in
  the run or inherited from a previously verified COMPLETE manifest with unchanged size — equal size alone is never
  proof; (C) canonical remote DB artifact `db/<run_id>/plan-estimate.sql.gz.age`, restore chain = encrypted SHA-256 →
  decrypt → gzip → isolated PostgreSQL restore → Alembic / schema check; (D) mandatory synthetic fixture = small

### Stage 14D.2A — PostgreSQL snapshot orchestration proof (2026-10-02, COMPLETE / OWNER ACCEPTED)

Narrow primitive only (no media backup, Oracle / R2 integration, manifest, `COMPLETE.json`, restore, `age`,
scheduling, credentials or cloud resources). Contract: `docs/STAGE_14D_BACKUP_RESTORE_PLAN.md` §7.1.

- **Added**: `backend/app/core/pg_snapshot_dump.py` (`snapshot_bound_dump`, `PgDumpCommand`, `run_dump_process`,
  typed `SnapshotDumpError` family) and `backend/app/domain/services/media_backup_ready_set.py` (READY-set v1
  serialization, `ready_set_digest`); tests `test_stage14d2a_ready_set.py`, `test_stage14d2a_dump_process.py`
  (local) and `test_stage14d2a_postgres.py` (opt-in real PostgreSQL proof A–G + version-mismatch refusal);
  `tests/pg_scratch_guard.py` gains `scratch_tool_prefix()` (`TEST_PG_TOOL_PREFIX` must be `docker exec [-i]` into a
  container whose name contains `scratch`).
- **Lifecycle**: dedicated exporter connection → pg_dump / server major-version equality check →
  `BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` → first statement `pg_export_snapshot()` → READY inventory in the
  same transaction → `pg_dump --snapshot` (tagged `PGAPPNAME`) → exporter released only after pg_dump exits. On
  failure / timeout / cancellation: child killed and reaped, tagged server backend terminated, exporter rolled back
  and closed, partial file removed, typed error.
- **Design refinement**: READY-set v1 adds a version header line (`plan-estimate/ready-set/v1`) before the sorted
  lines defined in 14D.1, with strict field rules (no normalization); the empty set has a fixed digest.
- **Local verification** (isolated CPython 3.12.14 venv from the pinned `requirements.txt`): 14D.2A local tests
  64 passed (PostgreSQL proof 9 skipped without opt-in env); full backend **2507 passed, 19 skipped, 0 failed**;
  mypy clean on the changed scope (6 files); Ruff clean; `git diff --check` clean. After the hardening below:
  14D.2A local tests **79 passed** (9 PostgreSQL skipped); full backend **2522 passed, 19 skipped, 0 failed**; mypy (7 files) and Ruff clean.
- **Owner-run real PostgreSQL proof — PASS (9 passed, 56.77 s)**: disposable container `pe-scratch-14d2a`
  (`postgres:16-alpine`, server 16.15, pg_dump 16.15, bound to 127.0.0.1:55433 only), CPython 3.12.14, pytest 8.4.2.
  A: server / pg_dump major 16/16, `ready_count` 3, dump → restore, restored READY count and digest equal the exporter
  snapshot. B: snapshot `ready_count` 2 while a fresh connection saw 4 after the concurrent committed insert +
  PENDING→READY transition; the restored dump stayed at 2; snapshot digest = restored digest, live digest differed —
  the mutation did not leak into either side. C: after the exporter ended PostgreSQL rejected the snapshot with
  SQLSTATE 22023 `invalid snapshot identifier`; pg_dump with the stale id returned rc 1. D: forced pg_dump failure
  (nonexistent role) rc 1, cleanup proven. E1 / E2: while pg_dump was lock-blocked the exporter was `idle in
  transaction` and the dump session `active` / `Lock`; after timeout and after cancellation no tagged session
  remained. F: zero READY assets → `ready_count` 0, `ready_set_sha256`
  `6e2b1178c1af4635f75bd0c77e7cce463e0e7055c120984e99ccf2d5a4922240` (= SHA-256 of the v1 header), restore verified.
  G: independent SQL and Python digests agreed regardless of query order. Extra: a pg_dump major-version mismatch was
  refused before any snapshot export.
- **Final review**: no defect in the proven semantics. Two hardening items fixed before commit (owner request):
  (1) the plaintext `.partial` dump is created with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` and mode 0600 plus `fchmod`, so it and the
  renamed final dump are owner-only whatever the process umask (no global umask change; refusal and cleanup semantics
  unchanged); (2) the dedicated exporter session is opened with `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=0` (session
  setting of a connection that exists only for this snapshot) and the value is re-read inside the snapshot
  transaction — anything other than `0` fails closed before the inventory or pg_dump. New tests: umask
  0000 / 0002 / 0022 / 0277 → final dump 0600; partial 0600 while being written under umask 0000; failure and
  existing-file refusal unchanged; exporter connect settings, statement order (export is the first statement in the
  transaction, release only after pg_dump) and fail-closed observed settings via a recording fake connection.
  Mutation check in a scratch copy: reverting either fix fails 5 resp. 3 tests. These changes do not alter the proven
  PostgreSQL semantics (see the 14D.2A report).
- **Second owner-run real PostgreSQL proof after hardening — PASS (9 passed, 55.48 s)**: `postgres:16-alpine`,
  server 16.15, pg_dump 16.15, CPython 3.12.14. Proofs A–G and the pg_dump major-version mismatch refusal all passed
  again on the hardened code; this also proves on real PostgreSQL 16.15 that the asyncpg startup setting
  `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=0` is accepted and does not invalidate the snapshot lifecycle. The private
  (0600) dump-file hardening is covered by the automated permission tests.
- **Temporary architecture**: the plaintext dump exists only locally and only until the later encrypted-dump stage,
  which gzips and `age`-encrypts it before anything leaves the VM.
- **Deferred**: dump SHA-256 is computed synchronously (move off the event loop for large dumps); a missing tool binary
  surfaces as `FileNotFoundError` rather than `SnapshotDumpError` (the exporter is still cleaned up); a second
  cancellation during the protected cleanup leaves it to finish in the background; the exporter holds ACCESS SHARE on
  `photo_assets` and the xmin horizon for the dump's duration, so backups must be kept from overlapping migrations
  operationally.
- **Status**: 14D.2A **COMPLETE / OWNER ACCEPTED** (2026-10-02). Stage 14D.2 as a whole remains **IN PROGRESS**. Production unchanged; uploads OFF; 14D.2B not started.

### Stage 14D.2B — encrypted database artifact primitive (2026-10-02 / 2026-10-03, COMPLETE / OWNER ACCEPTED)

Design audit approved with corrections (no application-side age-format parser; no production gzip round-trip).
Contract: `docs/STAGE_14D_BACKUP_RESTORE_PLAN.md` §9.1. No upload, manifest, restore, credentials, image change or

  identities).
- **Pipeline**: verified 0600 plaintext (14D.2A) → streaming in-process gzip (level 6, MTIME 0, no name / comment)
  → official `age --encrypt --recipient age1…` → 0600 exclusive `.partial` → age exit 0 → fsync → SHA-256 + size
  re-read from disk (worker thread) → rename → directory fsync → unlink plaintext → directory fsync. No gzip file;
  public recipients only; fixed minimal child environment; bounded stderr tail.
- **Backup-time success does not claim decryptability**; that is proven by the real-age round-trip (pending) and the
  14D.5 drill.
- **Fix found by tests during implementation**: opening a FIFO in place of the plaintext blocked the event loop;
  the plaintext is now opened with `O_NONBLOCK` (no effect on regular files) and refused as not regular.
- **Local verification** (isolated CPython 3.12.14 venv from the pinned `requirements.txt`): 14D.2B local tests
  **61 passed, 3 skipped** (real-age tests, `age` not installed on the development machine); 14D.2A regression

  `TEST_REAL_AGE=1 tests/test_stage14d2b_age_roundtrip.py`: **3 passed in 0.91 s**; combined 14D.2B suite
  (encryption + round-trip): **64 passed in 7.56 s, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Real decryptability proven with disposable
  identities (single recipient: decrypt → gunzip → exact original bytes; two recipients: identity A and identity B

### Stage 15E — inspection photo report as a PDF document (2026-10-08, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; backend only, no interface, no migration, no HTTP route)

The report follows the 14I read model (project photos → rooms → surfaces → openings → works → inspections → questions → findings), photos two to a row with a running number, date, caption and a legend of labelled markers; point markers (numbered red dots) and contours (white under-line + red line) are drawn from the stored fractions in the units of the printed picture; portrait photos are printed narrower (≤ 90 mm high).

An unreadable or missing photo, or one in another store, is an error — never a silent gap.

A wall without a size has "Dodaj wymiary" there; an archived wall is not edited; an empty / non-positive value is refused before anything is sent and the typed size stays; a server refusal shows its message and keeps the typed size. ### Stage 19F — adversarial check, cold-start decision, runbook and the full deployment script (2026-10-16, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — frontend + docs, no backend change, no migration, not deployed)
On the owner's word ("19f"). **Stage 19 is now complete locally and ready to deploy** (19B–19F).
- **Adversarial check (the main work):** three randomised, seeded, deterministic harnesses in the test suite:
  1. **What the phone shows = what the server will hold** (`offline/adversarial.test.ts`, 120 histories; one run of 800): notes, rooms and walls made, renamed, archived, restored and removed in a random order, **including records that exist only on the phone**; after **every** change the lists (with and without archived), every single record and the walls of every room read without a signal equal the model; after the sending the server holds exactly what the owner made.
  2. **Faults on the way** (80 histories; one run of 500): requests that never arrive, **answers lost after the server did the work**, 503 errors in the middle of the sending, the signal coming and going between tries — the server gets every change **once**, the outbox empties, nothing is refused.
  3. **Photo queue** (`utils/photoUploadQueue.adversarial.test.ts`, 60 histories; one run of 500): photos taken, cancelled and closed at random, the signal coming and going, **the application closed and opened again in the middle of an upload** — one upload at a time, never more than the limit, what rests on the phone is exactly what is not finished, **a photo the server already holds is never sent again**, with a steady signal everything that was not cancelled arrives. Six mutants of the queue were all killed by it.
- **Defects found and fixed (all real, all in the offline layer):** (a) **restoring a record that the list being read hides** (a room archived on the server, or made, archived and restored on the phone) did not bring it back into the list of active records until the synchronisation — the overlay now takes it from the saved list that shows archived records / from where an "archive" laid over the list took it out; (b) such a record did not return to **its place** in the server's order — the order of the whole list is now known (saved archived list + what was made); (c) a **change made to a record while it was archived** was lost when it was restored; (d) a file refused by the local checks (format, size) **took room in the 200 MB limit** while its row stayed on the screen. 13 + 4 regression tests added.
- **Cold-start decision (Q1 = A, recorded):** no service worker; work without a signal is for the **already opened** application; a Mini App closed in a basement cannot load its shell (a limit of Telegram, not of the application) — nothing is lost, the queue waits on the phone. A later stage can add it (its own plan: shell cache tied to the `?v=` cache-buster). The practical advice (do not close Telegram completely before going down) is in the runbook.

### Stage 19E — the screen of what waits, marks on records, small pictures of restored photos (2026-10-16, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — frontend only, no migration, not deployed)
On the owner's word ("19e").
- **Screen "Synchronizacja" (`SyncScreen`):** a full-screen sheet reached from the strip ("Szczegóły" appears as soon as a change, a refused change or a photo waits) and from the account window ("Synchronizacja (N)"; the window gives way to it). It shows, first, **"Wymagają uwagi (N)"** — the changes the server refused and the photos that failed — each with its kind and name ("Nowe pomieszczenie: Salon"), the time it was made, the **reason in words** (conflict / not found / invalid / server did not answer / a work status changed elsewhere — never the server's English text) and two actions: **"Ponów"** (back to waiting, attempts reset, the engine is asked to send) and **"Usuń zmianę"** (two taps; the warning says that changes depending on it may be refused); then **"Czekają na wysłanie (N)"** (every waiting change with its time) and **"Zdjęcia (N)"** (the photo rows with progress / cancel / retry); a note when there is no signal; **"Synchronizuj teraz"** (disabled without a signal or while sending: the engine sends at once and the photo queue is kicked); "Wszystko wysłane" when nothing waits. Telegram BackButton / Escape close it; the screens below suspend their own back button meanwhile (`showSync` in `App`). All 22 kinds of change have names in PL and RU (a test checks both languages against the list of kinds).

The overlay of 19C already carried `_pending`; the types now declare it. An inspection that waits can be opened and resumed, but not archived / reopened (only the server can) — the buttons are disabled.

### Stage 19C.3 — an inspection started without a signal, the status of a planned work, the order before acting on the server (2026-10-16, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — backend + frontend, no migration, not deployed)
On the owner's word ("19C. 3"). **Owner decision (asked, answered "the time from the phone, with a check"):** a work status marked without a signal is recorded with the moment of the tap.
- **Backend:**
  - **Inspections:** `POST …/inspections` takes the optional `id` chosen by the phone (UUIDv4); the same id with the same room, target, template, substrate, quality and notes returns the inspection already made (no second one), anything else on that id is `409 CLIENT_ID_CONFLICT`; a refused request leaves its id free.
  - **Statuses:** `PATCH …/work-plan/occurrences/{key}/execution` takes an optional `recorded_at` (the moment of the tap). `resolve_moment` (a pure rule in `work_execution_rules.py`) believes it only when it has a time zone, is not in the future (a skew of 2 min is clamped to now), is not older than 14 days and does not precede what is already recorded for that work (the later of `started_at` / `completed_at`); otherwise the server's own time is recorded as before. `started_at` / `completed_at` / `ready_after` still cannot be sent. The technological break and the calendar reminders follow the recorded moment (`ready_after` = real `completed_at` + break). A repeat of the same status is still a no-op (the first moment stays); a status changed elsewhere is still `409 WORK_EXECUTION_CONFLICT`. No migration.
- **Frontend (`writeRules`, `apiRequest`, outbox):**
  - Two new queueable writes: `inspection.create` and `execution.transition` (so 22 kinds in all). A new inspection is a `DRAFT` with no answers, in the list of its room and as a record of its own; its answers / findings are empty until the phone fills them; **the answers typed on the phone are now also laid over the inspection record** (the form is seeded from it — a gap of 19C: an inspection opened offline after its answers were saved offline used to show them empty). A status is laid over the work in the saved work plan (`execution` with the timestamps as the server records them, `ready_after` empty until the server answers) and gives the screen the answer in the shape of the server's.
  - `apiRequest` adds `recorded_at` to every status change (online too, so a repeat after a lost answer carries the same moment).
  - **"Prepare for work offline"** also reads the templates list of every substrate (starting an inspection asks for `?substrate=…`).
  - **Order before acting on the server (a gap of 19C found here):** a write that cannot be kept on the phone (estimate, contract, closing an inspection, bulk execution …) now first sends the changes waiting on the phone (the engine's `drainNow`), and goes on only when nothing waits any more; while there is no signal, or the sending stops on the way, it is **not made** and the owner reads "Zmiany zrobione bez zasięgu czekają jeszcze na wysłanie…" (`CHANGES_WAITING`). Before this, closing an inspection a second after the signal returned could close it without the answers still on the phone.
  - Closing an inspection without a signal says so in words ("Zakończenie badania wymaga połączenia z internetem. Odpowiedzi są zapisane na telefonie …"), the answers stay.
- **Tests:** backend 27 new (`test_stage19c3_offline_statuses.py`: the rule 8, the API 8, the inspection id 11); frontend: the rules (matching, overlay, resolve, optimistic result, labels), the whole way 8 (an inspection + answers + a status sent in order with the moment of the tap; a lost answer; a refused status parked; the order before closing; no request without a signal), the engine's runner 1, prepare 1, closing-without-signal messages 2. **Mutation check: 23 mutants killed** (10 backend, 13 frontend); one frontend mutant survived at first (the answer to a change laid over later changes) — a test with a started-reset-started sequence was added and it was killed.
- **Chromium (Playwright, 320 / 390 / 412 px, PL / RU):** two harnesses, 6 runs each, 0 problems: (1) a work started and marked done without a signal — the marks appear at once, "Zmiany czekające … 2", nothing reaches the server; when the signal returns two `PATCH`es arrive in order with `expected_status` IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED and `recorded_at` between the tap and the sending; (2) an inspection of a wall started offline (list from the phone, checklist opens, answer saved) — the server gets one `POST` with the id of the phone, then the `PUT` of the answers to that very id.
- **Full runs:** backend 5616 passed, 67 skipped (one environmental test of the passfile permissions, `test_workspace_preflight_passes_with_private_mounts_and_valid_passfile`, fails in this container as before and is left out); frontend 2790 passed (146 files; the one old uncaught error of `ProjectWorkspace.test.tsx` remains); `tsc` and `vite build` OK.
- **Not done:** the marks "~ po synchronizacji" on records and a screen of everything waiting / refused (19E); thumbnails of restored photos (19E); creating other things offline (estimates, contracts, protocols stay online-only by design).
- **To remember for the deployment:** the backend changed (two schemas, one rule, two services) — no migration, but a new backend image is needed; plus the full frontend deployment (19B changed `package.json`).

### Stage 19D — the photo queue on the phone (2026-10-16, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — frontend only, no migration, not deployed)
On the owner's word ("давай 19D"). **Closes the backlog item 14E.8** (the offline photo queue).
- **What changed for the owner:** a photo taken (camera or gallery) in a basement without a signal **waits on the phone** ("Czeka na zasięg — zdjęcie jest zapisane na telefonie" / "Ждёт связи — фото сохранено на телефоне") and is sent by itself when the signal returns; it also **survives closing the application**: the next time the application is opened and signed in, the queue is put back and goes on sending. The photo buttons stay while the server cannot be reached (the last answer about the photo storage is kept); the list of photos of the server is then replaced by a calm note instead of a red error.
- **Storage:** IndexedDB database version 3: `photos` (the facts about a photo: owner, target, `upload_id`, name, type, size, state, attempts, the reason of a failure) and `photoFiles` (its bytes as an `ArrayBuffer`, kept apart so that a change of state does not rewrite up to 25 MB; a `Blob` is not copied faithfully by every WebView and by the test environment). Written when the photo is queued, updated when an upload starts / fails / is retried, **removed when it is sent, cancelled or closed**. A photo that the checks refuse at once (format / size) is not kept. If the phone cannot keep it (disk full, no IndexedDB) the row says so and the photo is still sent while the application stays open.
- **Queue (`photoUploadQueue.ts`):** new `store`, `canStart`, `refreshSession`, `limitBytes` options; `restore()` (oldest first, ahead of new photos; bytes stay in storage until the upload starts, so a long queue does not fill the memory; after a failure or a pause the bytes leave the memory again); `kick()`.
  - **Waits** while there is no signal (`canStart` = the connection is not known to be lost **and** no older change waits in the outbox — a photo may belong to a room or a wall made without a signal; a refused (failed) change does not hold photos back). `kick()` is called when the connection or the outbox counts change.
  - **No signal in the middle of an upload:** a transport failure whose server check gets no answer puts the photo back to waiting with nothing counted against it; later the server is asked first (`GET` by `upload_id`): found → done, not found → sent again with the **same** `upload_id` (backend idempotency, Stage 14). A photo restored after a restart that had a POST started is checked the same way before it is sent.
  - **Limit (Q3):** 200 MB of photos waiting (queued / uploading / failed — a failed one keeps its room until it is closed; a sent one frees it); more files of a selection are left out and the owner is told ("kolejka … jest pełna (200 MB)"); a warning from 160 MB (80 %). A photo the checks refuse does not use up the room.
  - **Token expired while the photo waited:** the engine signs in again with Telegram `initData` (the same function as the sync engine) and sends once more; a second refusal fails the queue with the session message as before.
  - A photo whose bytes are gone from the phone fails with its own message (`gone_from_phone`).
- **Owner:** each record belongs to the owner who is signed in; another owner signing in wipes everything (including photos) and the queue in memory lets go (`onOfflineDataCleared`); "Wyczyść dane offline" warns about waiting photos ("zdjęcia niewysłane … zostaną utracone (N)"). "Przygotuj do pracy offline" also reads the photo-storage status, so the buttons are there without a signal.
- **UI:** `PhotoUploadQueueList` (name from the item, waiting-for-signal text, "not saved on the phone" hint), `PhotoSection` (picker stays offline, queue-full and nearly-full notes, calm "list unavailable" note), `usePhotoStorage.usable`, `AccountModal`, locales PL / RU (`photos.queue.*`, `photos.picker.queue_full`, `photos.section.offline_list_note`, `photos.errors.gone_from_phone`, `offline.clear_pending_photos`).
- **Tests:** new — queue with a store 22, IndexedDB store 6, whole way across a restart 4 (a photo survives the closing, waits for the signal and for the outbox, is looked up first when its POST had been started, another owner does not see it), sign-in puts the queue back 1, `PhotoSection` without a signal 4, account window 1; old tests adapted (`name` / `size` fields). **Mutation check:** 19 mutants killed (no wait for the signal, no wait for the outbox, no limit, no GET-first, a sent photo kept, token loop, memory not released, no restore order, no restore at sign-in, storage not wiped, …); the one for the sign-in restore first "survived" only because no test existed — a test was added and the mutant killed. One old test (`SurfaceExecutionView.photos`) needed the connection state set to "reachable": its un-mocked calendar requests found no server and marked the application "no signal", which now (correctly) holds the queue.
- **Full runs:** frontend 2762 passed (145 files; the one old uncaught error of `ProjectWorkspace.test.tsx` remains), `tsc --noEmit` and `vite build` OK; the backend is untouched since 19C (5589 passed, 67 skipped).
- **Chromium (Playwright, 320 / 390 / 412 px, PL / RU):** 6 runs, 0 problems — a photo chosen while the API is unreachable stays in IndexedDB and is not sent; after a **reload** the same photo is sent once with the same `upload_id` and its bytes, then nothing is left on the phone; no horizontal overflow.
- **Not done (next sub-stages):** a place to see all waiting photos at once and the refused ones (19E: the strip counts only outbox changes now); thumbnails of photos restored after a restart (a grey placeholder with the name until they are sent); cold start without a signal (Q1 = A: not in scope); statuses of works and starting an inspection without a signal (19C.3 if the owner wants it).
- **Deployment note:** frontend only, but `package.json` changed in 19B, so Stage 19 needs the full deployment script (19F).

### Stage 19C — changes made without a signal: client ids, the outbox, the sync engine (2026-10-15 / 16, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — backend + frontend, no migration, not deployed)
On the owner's word ("давай 19C"; `stage-19` pushed with 19B).
- **19C.1 backend — an id chosen by the phone.** The create routes of rooms, surfaces, openings, rectangles of the floor / ceiling and notes take an optional `id` (a random UUIDv4 only). A create under it is **idempotent**: the same id with the same parent and content returns the record already made (no second floor / ceiling, an opening is not counted against the wall twice); the id taken by anything else (other content, parent or owner) is `409 {code: CLIENT_ID_CONFLICT}`; a request that failed leaves its id free. No migration (keys are already UUID). 17 new tests.
- **19C.2 frontend — what the phone does.**
  - `outbox` (IndexedDB store, database version 2): every change keeps its method, path, body, kind, label, status (`pending` / `failed`), attempts and the server's reason; the order of making is the order of sending; only the signed-in owner's changes are seen.
  - **What can be written without a signal:** notes (create / edit / remove), rooms, walls and other surfaces, openings, rectangles of the floor / ceiling (create / edit / archive / restore), and the answers of an inspection (`PUT`). Everything else (estimate, PDF, contract, protocols, price book, calendar, wall generation, completing an inspection, photos) needs the server as before.
  - **`apiRequest`:** a create gets an id chosen on the phone at once (online too, so a lost answer can be repeated safely); while the server is known to be out of reach, or older changes still wait (the order is kept), or the request fails / hangs for 20 s, the change is **kept** and the screen gets the record at once, marked `_pending`. Reads are answered from the phone at once while offline (no waiting for a hanging request), with the waiting changes **laid over** the saved copy; a record or a list of a room / wall made on the phone is built from the outbox. A refusal of the server (4xx) is raised as before and nothing is kept.
  - **Sync engine:** one sending at a time, in order, with the token; removes a change when accepted; stops when the network is gone (nothing lost); a refusal (422 / 409 / …) is parked as `failed` with the reason and the rest goes on; 5xx / 429 are tried again up to 5 times; a `DELETE` of something already gone counts as done; an expired token is renewed from the data Telegram gives the open Mini App (`initData`) and the same change is sent again, else "sign in again" is shown. It starts at the application start, when the signal returns, 0.3 s after a change and every 30 s while something waits.
  - **Strips:** "Zmiany czekające na wysłanie: N" / "Wysyłam…" / "Serwer odrzucił zmiany: N" / "Wysłano zmian: N" + a refresh button (a minute) / "sign in again". "Wyczyść dane offline" warns when unsent changes exist; another owner signing in removes everything (Q8).
- **Tests:** 130+ new on the frontend (rules 58, outbox 8, `apiRequest` queue 14, sync engine 16, whole way 4, strips 7, account window 2); 8 mutants killed (no id, no order, a sent change kept, `DELETE` 404, refused changes laid over, a refusal stops the queue, the clean-up keeps the outbox, no instant read offline). **Chromium 320 / 390 / 412 px, PL and RU: a note written with the requests aborted → shown at once with the strips → the signal returns → the server received exactly one `POST` with a UUIDv4 `id` and the text → "Wysłano zmian"** (12 checks, 0 problems).
- **Not done (next):** statuses of works (`Realizacja`) and starting an inspection without a signal (an inspection create needs a client id too), the marks "~ po synchronizacji" on records and the screen of refused changes (19E), photos (19D). Derived numbers (areas, totals) of a record made on the phone appear after the sending (Q5 b: the typed sizes are shown).

### Stage 19B — storage on the phone, read cache, connection strip, "Przygotuj do pracy offline" (2026-10-15, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — frontend only, no migration, not deployed)
Started on the owner's answers (Q1 = A, Q3 = 200 MB, the rest by recommendation); plan v2.
- **Storage:** IndexedDB database `plan-estimate-offline` (library `idb` 8.0.4, tests `fake-indexeddb` 6.2.5 — **`package.json` / `package-lock.json` changed, so the release needs the full deployment script, not the frontend-only one**): `readCache` (key `owner|path`, copy + time) and `meta`. The owner is remembered at sign-in (`offline_owner`); **another owner signing in removes everything first (Q8)**; copies not saved again for 30 days are purged at start (Q10); where the browser has no IndexedDB everything works as before.
- **Read cache in `apiRequest`:** GET of the kept kinds only (the object and its list, the summary, notes, rooms and everything under them — surfaces, openings, rectangles, inspections with answers, work plans, risks — clients, checklist templates; **never** photos, documents, estimates, contract / protocols, price book, calendar, knowledge base, authentication) is saved after every answer of the server; on a **network failure** (a `TypeError`, or 12 s without an answer — a weak signal hangs instead of failing) the last copy is returned; a server error answer (4xx / 5xx) is always shown as it is, never replaced by a copy. Writes are never kept or served (19C). `fetchClients` / `fetchClient` now go through `apiRequest` (they used their own `fetch`).
- **Connection:** known from the requests themselves (not `navigator.onLine`, which lies in a basement) plus the browser's events; while offline the server is looked at (`/api/health`) every 15 s, so the strip goes away by itself. A strip under the header appears only when offline or when a saved copy is on screen: "Brak połączenia — pokazuję dane zapisane na telefonie (z HH:MM)".
- **"Przygotuj do pracy offline"** under the tiles of an object: one request at a time — object, summary, notes, clients, checklist templates, rooms, surfaces, rectangles, openings of the walls, work plans (404 is not a failure), inspections with answers — with the progress "12 / 40", the result, the time of the last preparation; disabled without a connection. **"Wyczyść dane offline"** in the account window (second tap confirms).
- **Tests:** 82 new (cache rules 38, store 7, `apiRequest` cache 10, connection and watching 7, preparation 5, strip 5, button 5, account window 3, hub 1); frontend 2621 passed (the one old uncaught error of `ProjectWorkspace.test.tsx` stays); `tsc` and `vite build` also from a copy of `frontend/` without `backend/`. **Chromium 320 / 390 / 412 px, PL and RU, a real loss of the signal (requests aborted as `internetdisconnected`): 24 checks, 0 problems** — prepare online → lose the signal → the list of objects, the object, its rooms and a room with walls / floor / ceiling open from the phone with the strip and the time → the signal returns → the strip goes away.
- **Not done (next sub-stages):** writing without a signal (19C), photos (19D), the synchronisation screen (19E); a cold start without a signal (Q1 = A: not in scope).

### Stage 19A — offline drafts: audit and plan (2026-10-15, DOCUMENT ONLY — branch `stage-19`)
Started on the owner's word ("начинай Stage 19") after the acceptance of Stage 18 and its merge into `main` (`2a4cad3`).
- **Audit** (`docs/STAGE_19_OFFLINE_DRAFTS_PLAN_RU.md`, section 2): the browser storage is `localStorage` only (token, language, a few defaults), no IndexedDB, no service worker; all requests go through one `apiRequest` without any cache or queue; the photo upload queue (14E) is in memory by decision D2 but already has a stable `upload_id`; entity ids are UUIDs issued by the server (create routes take no client `id`), derived numbers (areas, totals) are computed on the server; no versions / ETag, only `updated_at`; JWT lives 7 days and the app re-logs in by `initData`. The usual field scenario is an app that is ALREADY OPEN when the signal is lost — it does not need a service worker; a cold start without a signal does (and may not work in Telegram on iPhone — to check on devices).
- **Proposed architecture:** IndexedDB (`idb`) with a read cache (stale-while-revalidate for GETs), an outbox of operations sent in order when the signal returns, optional client `id` on the create routes (idempotent, no migration), a persistent photo queue (closes 14E.8), an indicator and a "synchronisation" screen with a list of what needs attention; estimate, PDF, contract, protocols, price book and calendar stay online-only.
- **Sub-stages proposed:** 19B storage + cache + indicator, 19C client ids + outbox + sync engine, 19D photo queue, 19E screens, 19F adversarial check + cold-start decision + runbook. **Questions to the owner:** Q1–Q15 with recommendations.

### Stage 18F — the adversarial check, the runbook and the deployment scripts (2026-10-15, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — nothing deployed)
Started on the owner's word ("пуш и начинай 18F"; `stage-18` pushed at `e84c132`).
- **What the check found and fixed (each with a test that fails without the fix):**
  - **Two passes meeting on one fact** (the 10-minute reconciliation and a user's request on the same object): the second insert would have failed on the unique key and rolled back the user's own action. Now `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; proven on PostgreSQL with eight simultaneous passes (0 duplicates).
  - **A queue of reminders that must wait** (quiet hours, the messages switched off) hid the ones behind it (a page of 100 rows): found by the load measurement. Now the pass goes page by page (keyset on time and id, up to 20 pages).
  - **The master switch** ("Telegram messages") did not hold back the owner's own reminders: now it does (they stay pending until the switch is on or they are a day old).
  - **Damaged data:** a date at the end of time or a garbage date in the answers of a contract stopped the whole calendar; now the term is dropped and the rest goes on. A term of the contract above ten years is a typo and gives nothing.
  - **A flood of own reminders:** at most 200 waiting per owner (`TOO_MANY`, text PL / RU).
- **Checked and found right:** the morning digest at the same wall-clock hour on every day of two years in every zone of the list (7), the quiet-hours shift never goes back in time, the time that does not exist (spring) or happens twice (autumn) does not break anything; the edges of a day and of the quiet hours; a deadline moved after its week-ahead notice was sent (history stays, the rest is withdrawn, the new date is announced in full); an archived surface takes its break reminder with it and brings it back when restored; the whole cycle over every source twice changes nothing the second time.
- **Load (PostgreSQL 16, throwaway native cluster, no Docker):** 40 objects, 2400 works, 1080 reminders: reconciliation of all objects 1.6 s (0.4 s when nothing changes), the agenda 0.35 s, a dispatcher pass over 100 due reminders 0.33 s, the process stays near 90 MB.

### Stage 17F.1 — the pinned header (2026-10-11, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — frontend only)
Stage 17E.1 + 17C.3 were deployed and the owner's phone check passed ("Все PASS"); one visible defect: the header with the menu scrolled away with the page.
- **Cause:** the header was already `sticky top-0` (Stage 16K), but the application's outer block had `overflow-x-hidden`. `overflow-x: hidden` makes a block a scroll container, so the sticky header stuck to that block (which never scrolls: it grows with its content) and not to the screen. Reproduced in Chromium before the fix: after scrolling 3984 px the header was at `top = -3984`.
- **Fix:** `overflow-x-hidden` -> `overflow-x-clip` on the outer block (cuts the same horizontal overflow, creates no scroll container; `body { overflow-x: hidden }` in `index.css` propagates to the screen and does not interfere); a hairline under the header so scrolled content does not look cut off beneath it. Full-screen windows (menu z-40, dialogs and photo viewers z-50 and higher) stay above the header (z-30).
- **Tests:** `App.test.tsx` — the header is `sticky top-0` and no ancestor of it has `overflow-(x|y)-(hidden|auto|scroll)` (the mutant "hidden again" fails it); in Chromium (320 / 390 / 412 px): after scrolling 3.6–4.0 thousand px the header is at `top = 0`, the menu opens while scrolled, no horizontal overflow. Frontend 2382 passed, `tsc`, `vite build`.
- **Production:** frontend only, no backend, no migration: `docs/STAGE_17_DEPLOY_FRONTEND_ONLY_RU.sh`.

### Stage 16J — the adversarial check of the whole of Stage 16, the migrations, the runbook (2026-10-11, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; no new migration)
Last sub-stage of Stage 16 (owner: "пуш и делаем 16J"; 16I.4 pushed as `3b5b5d0`). Nothing new for the user; the whole stage was attacked and prepared for the deployment.
- **Found and fixed (a real bug):** the remarks of an acceptance protocol kept their order only because a Python dict does; PostgreSQL JSONB does **not** keep the order of the keys of an object, so on the real database the remarks of a surface would come back sorted by their id. Now every new remark gets a `position` (1 + the largest on the surface), `ordered_remarks` sorts by `(position, id)`, and the read model, the document and the frozen snapshot all use it.
- **Adversarial matrix** (`tests/test_stage16j_adversarial.py`, 7 tests): every route of Stage 16 is taken from `app.openapi()` (62 routes of contracts, representatives, adjacent works, handover, concealed works, acceptance, decisions, downtime and the documents): without a token → 401; with **another owner's** project → only 404 / 422, never 200 and no name of the project in the answer (≥ 50 refusals); the owner's own lists → 200; a project that does not exist → 404.
- **Big documents** (the real renderer, the limits of the production process): acceptance of 60 surfaces / 120 remarks → 46 pages, 97 KB, 6.0 s; decisions of 30 items → 16 pages, 45 KB, 3.2 s; downtime of 60 days → 4 pages, 21 KB, 1.9 s; the number stands on every page; every file is far below 5 MB; the tests fix the limits.
- **Migrations `0038 → 0053 → 0038 → 0053` on PostgreSQL 16** (a scratch cluster): 15 up / 15 down / 15 up; a prod-like journal row of Stage 15 survives; the allowed kinds after `0053`: ESTIMATE, PHOTO_REPORT, TECH_CARD, PRODUCTION_PLAN, CONTRACT, HANDOVER_PROTOCOL, CONCEALED_WORKS_PROTOCOL, FINAL_PROTOCOL, DECISION_PROTOCOL, DOWNTIME_NOTICE, DOWNTIME_PROTOCOL; `alembic` autogenerate shows only the differences that existed before Stage 16; downgrades refuse while evidence exists.
- **Infrastructure compared with production (`origin/main` = `848d360`):** `docker-compose.prod.yml`, `Caddyfile`, `Dockerfile`s, `entrypoint.sh`, `requirements*`, `package*.json` and `app/backup` — **no difference**; only `backend/alembic/versions/0039…0053` (15 files) among the infrastructure paths. The catalogues and templates travel inside `backend/app`.
- **Runbook:** `docs/STAGE_16_PRODUCTION_RUNBOOK_RU.md` (D1–D4 decisions, A0 read-only, A1 backup, A2 code, A3 build with `:pre-16` tags, A3b smoke in the new image (catalogues, renderer, head `0053`), GATE M with the migration assessment, A4 backend, A4b Telegram, A5 frontend, A6 menu button, A7 the owner's check of every card on the phone (PL / RU, 320–412 px), A8 time and memory of the biggest document, A9 rebuild of the backup images and a full backup, closing conditions, the risk table and the rollback).

### Stage 16I.3 — the notice and the protocol of downtime on the customer's side: data, rules, API, documents (2026-10-11, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; migration `0053_downtime_episodes`)
Third step of 16I (owner: "пуш и продолжаем"; 16I.2 pushed as `2491a65`). Annex 8 of the contract and requirement А5: what the customer owes stops the work (no access, the premises not ready, no utilities, other contractors not finished, no decision, materials not delivered, a stop order — the contract's own list, `§ 10 ust. 1`), the contractor **notifies** at once with photos (`§ 10 ust. 2`), and when the obstacle stays, a **protocol** confirms the days and the sum for readiness.
- **One episode, two documents (`downtime_episodes`):** one row per downtime of one object (`sequence` per object). States `DRAFT` (the notice is written) → `NOTICED` (the notice is issued and frozen; the protocol is written) → `CLOSED` (the protocol is issued and frozen), or `ARCHIVED` when the obstacle goes away (an issued notice stays in the journal as it was sent). **At most one episode is open** (a draft or a noticed one) per object. The notice's entries change only while a draft, the protocol's only once noticed.
- **The notice:** the cause (the new catalogue `downtime_causes.json`, the eight causes of the contract, PL / RU names), a note (obligatory for "other"), the rooms (none = the whole object), the day and time of the notice, the way it was sent (the documentary form), **the photos** (those of the object as a whole and of the chosen rooms and their surfaces; changing the rooms drops the photos that no longer belong; archived rooms and surfaces offer none), what the contractor needs and until when. Blockers in the order of doing: executor profile, client, an issued or signed contract, the cause (and its note), the day, what is needed, **at least one photo** (the notice goes with photos).
- **The protocol:** the days of downtime — each **after the day of the notice and a working day** (Monday to Friday; the calendar of public holidays is not kept), each once, with the answer **whether other work could be done** that day (such a day is no downtime day and is not paid for) and a note; the day and time of the protocol, the people present, the effect on the deadline **in the owner's words**, the refusal to sign (always with its notes), notes. Blockers: the days, the day of the protocol (no day later than it), the people present, the notes of a refusal.
- **The sum for readiness is derived, never typed:** the rate per day times the days without other work, **not more than the cap** (a percentage of the estimated remuneration), all from **the frozen contract the notice was written under** (a newer contract does not change it); a rate, a cap or a total the contract leaves empty stays empty (the document prints a line to fill in); the limit of days is the contract's own and only says whether the downtime has run past it. Amounts are rounded half-up to the grosz.
- **API:** `GET / POST /api/projects/{id}/downtimes` (opens or returns the open episode), `GET / PATCH …/{id}`, `POST …/{id}/archive`, `POST …/{id}/issue-notice`, `POST …/{id}/issue-protocol`, working versions `POST …/documents/downtime-notice/preview` and `…/downtime-protocol/preview` (pale watermark, no number, no journal row, never refuse; blank forms with the causes to tick and five empty rows for the days); the read model carries the cause's name, the days with their weekday, the settlement (rate, amount, cap, whether capped, payable, the limit), the chosen photos and the options, the rooms and the blockers of the **next** document; refusals 422 `DOWNTIME_INVALID` (field and reason: `NOTICE_FROZEN`, `NOT_NOTICED_YET`, `BAD_DAY`, `UNKNOWN_CAUSE` ...), 409 `DOWNTIME_NOT_EDITABLE`, 422 `DOWNTIME_GATE_BLOCKED` (takes no number), 404.
- **The pages:** the notice (`downtime_notice.html.j2`, prefix `ZAWPRZ`): the object, the rooms, the day, time and way of notice, the contract; all eight causes as boxes (the chosen one checked); the photos (number, time, caption, room, reference); what is needed and until when; the pointer to § 10 ust. 2. The protocol (`downtime_protocol.html.j2`, prefix `PROPRZ`): the notice it follows (number and day), the cause, the rooms, the day of the protocol, the people present, the days with weekday and the answer about other work, the totals (days, days without other work, the rate, the sum — with the sentence about the cap when it applied), the pointer to § 10 ust. 2 and 3, the effect on the deadline, the refusal to sign, notes, signatures. Both come from the stored page when sent again (`DOWNTIME_NOT_ISSUED` when it is missing).
- **Journal and frontend:** two new journal kinds `DOWNTIME_NOTICE` and `DOWNTIME_PROTOCOL`; the frontend knows their names, the error sentence and the catalogue's names of the causes (PL / RU).
- **Database:** `0053_downtime_episodes` — the table with its CHECKs (statuses, sequence, **a noticed or closed episode always has its frozen notice, a closed one its frozen protocol**), one open episode per object, a number once per object, the widened journal CHECK; reversible, the downgrade **refuses while an episode or a journal row of these kinds exists**. Checked on PostgreSQL 16: a closed and a noticed episode are accepted, a second open one, a repeated number, a wrong status or sequence, a noticed episode without its notice and a closed one without its protocol are refused, both new journal kinds are accepted and another is refused, the downgrade is refused with data, then works, the upgrade restores.
- **Tests:** backend `test_stage16i3_downtime` 34 (the entries and each refusal by name and reason, the gating by state, the days and their rules, the blockers, the sum with the cap / empty rate / rounding / limit, the episode with the photos following the rooms, foreign data, both pages with every part, the cap sentence, the refusal to sign, blank forms, real PDFs, both gates and "no number", both freezes with snapshots, pages unchanged when the data change, empty stored pages, both previews, the sum following the contract of the notice, archived rooms' photos, HTTP 401 / 404 / 409 / 422 / 202 through the whole life, an abandoned noticed episode, the catalogue, the registry, the migration); `test_stage16b3_catalog` extended. **Mutation check:** 24 mutants of the rules, the sum, the pages, the service, the issuer and the photo source; every one killed or shown equivalent (two survivors — the contract of the notice and the archived rooms' photos — got tests).
- **Visual check:** the issued notice (1 page), the issued protocol (2 pages) and the blank forms were rendered to PDF and looked at.
- **Full runs:** backend 5213 passed, 67 skipped, 1 known sandbox-root preflight failure (`test_stage14d2c_preflight`, fails identically without this change); frontend 2236 passed (one test extended for the two new journal kinds), `tsc` clean, `vite build` OK.
- **Not in this step:** the phone screen (16I.4); the calendar of public holidays (a Saturday and Sunday are refused, a holiday is not); the "request to remove the obstacle with the threat of withdrawal" (`§ 10 ust. 5`) — the read model only says that the limit of days is past; the link of the downtime to the production plan.
- **Next:** 16I.4 — only after the owner's "делаем 16I.4" (or "продолжаем").

### Stage 16I.1 — the protocol of information and decisions of the customer: data, rules, API, document (2026-10-10, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; migration `0052_decision_protocols`)
First step of 16I (owner: "пуш и продолжаем"; 16H.3 pushed as `89438d6`; 16I split into 16I.1 this protocol, 16I.2 its phone screen, 16I.3 the downtime notice and protocol, 16I.4 its screen). Annex 9 of the contract: when the contractor recommends a technological solution and the customer gives it up or demands the work against it, the parties write down what was recommended, the risk in plain language, the decision, who was present (contract `executor_recommendations`, § 17).
- **Data (`decision_protocols`):** one row per sitting of one object (`sequence` per object, one `DRAFT` per object, `DRAFT` → `ISSUED` (frozen) → `ARCHIVED`); the day and time, the people present, an **ordered list of items**, the customer's declaration that he understood and could ask, a refusal to sign (with its circumstances in the notes), notes; frozen columns as in the other protocols. An item is **a risk of the application** (active, `warranty_exclusion_candidate`; its texts — what was found, the recommendation, the consequences — are the built-in Polish risk catalogue's and cannot be edited) **or a recommendation of the contractor's own** (room, title, recommendation, consequences, price). Each item carries the **decision**: accepts the recommendation (with the number of the order), gives it up, or **insists on the work against it** — and then the contractor's answer: performs it after the protocol, or refuses (§ 17 ust. 3). The answer exists only with a demand, the order number only with an acceptance.
- **Rules (`domain/protocols/decision.py`), deterministic:** every entry is checked by name and reason (a risk must be an active candidate of this object; the risk of an item is never changed — remove and add; a new own item needs its three texts; the room must be the object's; money normalised); blockers in the order of doing: executor profile, client, an issued or signed contract, the day, people present, at least one item, **a risk that is no longer found**, an item without a decision, a demand without the contractor's answer, **the declaration or the refusal to sign** (a refusal always needs its notes). What a decision means for the guarantee is **not** said by the application: the page points at § 16 ust. 3 lit. f of the contract.
- **API:** `GET / POST /api/projects/{id}/decisions`, `GET / PATCH …/{id}`, `POST …/{id}/archive`, `POST …/{id}/issue`; the read model resolves every item to its texts, offers the risks that may be added (`risk_options`, with `used`), the rooms, the blockers and the contract; refusals 422 `DECISION_INVALID` (field and reason), 409 `DECISION_NOT_EDITABLE`, 422 `DECISION_GATE_BLOCKED` (takes no number), 404.
- **The page (`decision_document.py`, `decision_protocol.html.j2`, version `1`, number prefix `DECYZ`):** the object, the day and time, the contract, the people present; for every item: the room, what was found, the recommendation (and its price), the risk and its possible consequences, the three decision boxes (the chosen one checked), the contractor's position when the customer insists, the pointer to the contract for a decision that gives up or overrules, a note; the declaration and the refusal to sign as boxes; notes; signatures. Working version `POST …/documents/decision/preview` — pale watermark, no number, no journal row, never refuses; with no draft it is a blank form with three empty items.
- **Issue and journal:** `DECISION_PROTOCOL` is a new journal kind (CHECK widened in the same migration); the freeze keeps the items with their resolved texts and decisions, the people, the contract and the exact page; the PDF is made again from the stored page (`DECISION_NOT_ISSUED` when it is missing); the frontend knows the kind label and the error (PL / RU).
- **Database:** `0052_decision_protocols` — the table with its CHECKs, one draft per object, a number once per object, the widened journal CHECK; reversible, the downgrade **refuses while a protocol or a journal row of this kind exists**. Checked on PostgreSQL 16 (see the PASS report).
- **Tests:** backend `test_stage16i1_decisions` 26 (the entries and each refusal by name and reason, items of both kinds and their order, the locks on risk items, decisions and the contractor's answer, removal and "a failed change changes nothing", every blocker and the order, the declaration / refusal rules, only active candidate risks of the object offered with the catalogue's texts, the read model, a risk that stops being found, the draft's life and foreign data, the page with every part, a refusal to sign, the blank form and "cannot be numbered", a real PDF, the gate and "no number", the freeze with the snapshot, the frozen page unchanged, the empty stored page, the preview, HTTP 401 / 404 / 409 / 422 / 202, the registry, the migration). **Mutation check:** 19 mutants of the rules, the source query, the page and the issuer, all killed.
- **Visual check:** the issued protocol (2 pages) and the blank form were rendered to PDF and looked at.
- **Full runs:** backend 5179 passed, 67 skipped, 1 known sandbox-root preflight failure (`test_stage14d2c_preflight`, fails identically without this change); frontend 2216 passed (one test extended for the new journal kind), `tsc` clean, `vite build` OK; the migration checked on PostgreSQL 16: one draft, a number once, a wrong status / sequence / an issued row without its page and a wrong journal kind are refused, the new kind and a frozen issued row are accepted, the downgrade is refused with data, then works, the upgrade restores.
- **Not in this step:** the phone screen (16I.2); the downtime notice and protocol (16I.3 / 16I.4); the effect of a decision on the risk's later life (no link yet); photos in the protocol.
- **Next:** 16I.2 — only after the owner's "делаем 16I.2" (or "продолжаем").

### Stage 16H.2 — the acceptance protocol as a document: page, issuing, working version (2026-10-10, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; migration `0051_final_protocol_kind`)
Second step of 16H (owner: "Пуш и 16H. 2"; 16H.1 pushed as `ff68e18`). The protocol of 16H.1 becomes a printable, numbered, frozen document, like the handover and concealed works protocols.
- **The page (`acceptance_document.py`, `acceptance_protocol.html.j2`, version `1`, number prefix `ODBIOR`):** the title follows the scope — "Protokół odbioru końcowego" / "… częściowego" (and "… odbioru prac" for a blank form); the object, the scope (a partial one names its rooms), the day and time, the contract (version and number); the people present **or**, for an absent customer, the sentence with **both** notification days (pointing at § 14 ust. 5); the conditions of the assessment of every standard in scope (the catalogue's text) with the agreed conditions and the instruments used (catalogue names); per surface its standard, its planned works with their state (the execution of Stage 13: wykonana / w trakcie / niewykonana) and **the derived result**; the list of remarks (surface, place, description, class, deadline, short references of the defect photos) with the legend of the two classes (the catalogue's text); the result as three boxes (the derived one checked); the settlement (amount due, amount retained, batches), the instructions handed over, notes; signatures. Photos are **listed, not embedded**.
- **Working version:** `POST /api/projects/{id}/documents/acceptance/preview` — pale watermark, no number, no journal row, never refuses; follows the open draft or is a blank form (empty rows for surfaces and for six remarks, empty boxes, empty lines), to fill in by hand at the wall.
- **Issue:** `POST /api/projects/{id}/acceptances/{aid}/issue` → 202 + journal `ODBIOR/…`; the gate refuses with the list (422 `ACCEPTANCE_GATE_BLOCKED`) and **takes no number**; then the freeze (snapshot: scope kind, derived result, rooms, conditions, surfaces with the works and their state, remarks with the captions of the photos, people present, notification days, amounts, the contract; the exact page) and the PDF made again from the stored page whenever it is needed (`ACCEPTANCE_NOT_ISSUED` when the page is missing).
- **Registry and journal:** `FINAL_PROTOCOL` is a real template now. It was the last skeleton of 15G, so **the skeleton engine is removed** (`skeleton_document.py`, `skeleton.html.j2`, its CSS, labels, tests, `SKELETON_*` in the registry, the frontend sentence for `SKELETON_SECTION_UNKNOWN`): every kind of document has its own template. The journal kind is `FINAL_PROTOCOL`; the frontend knows the kind label and the error `ACCEPTANCE_NOT_ISSUED` (PL / RU).

### Stage 16H.1 — the protocol of acceptance of the work: data, rules, API (2026-10-10, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; migration `0050_acceptance_protocols`)
First step of 16H (owner: "Пуш и дальше"; split 16H.1 data / rules / API, 16H.2 document and issuing with the journal kind `FINAL_PROTOCOL`, 16H.3 the phone screen). The final or partial acceptance of the work by the algorithm of plan § 5.
- **Data (`acceptance_protocols`):** one row per acceptance (`sequence` per object, one `DRAFT` per object, `DRAFT` → `ISSUED` (frozen) → `ARCHIVED`); the day and time, the people present **or** "the customer did not come" with **two** notification days (contract § 14 ust. 5), the rooms in scope, the conditions note, the instruments used (catalogue keys), per surface: assessed + remarks (place, description, class **removable / significant**, a deadline for a removable one, photos), batches, instructions given, the amount due and the amount retained (text "1234.50"), notes. Frozen columns (time, snapshot, page, contract id / version) as in the other protocols.
- **Rules (`domain/protocols/acceptance.py`), deterministic, the result is **derived, never typed**:** a surface is *not accepted* when any planned work is not `COMPLETED` in the execution of Stage 13 or it has a significant remark; *accepted with remarks* when it has only removable remarks (each with its deadline); otherwise *accepted*; the whole is the worst of its surfaces. The kind is `FINAL` when the chosen rooms are all rooms with planned works, else `PARTIAL`. The conditions of the assessment come per standard from `evaluation_conditions.json`; a standard that needs agreed conditions (S4) needs the conditions note. A remark's photo must be a **DEFECT photo of that very surface**; money is normalised; people are copied by name from the register.
- **Blockers, in the order of doing:** executor profile, client, an issued or signed contract, scope (a room with planned works), the day, the notification days of an absent customer (both, the second after the first, the acceptance not before the second), people present, the conditions note, every surface in scope assessed.
- **API:** `GET / POST /api/projects/{id}/acceptances`, `GET / PATCH …/{aid}`, `POST …/{aid}/archive`; the read model carries the rooms with their number of surfaces, the surfaces with their works, `incomplete`, remarks and photo options, the derived `scope_kind` and `result`, `conditions`, `blockers`, the contract; refusals 422 `ACCEPTANCE_INVALID` (field and reason; a remark deadline sent as text is read as an ISO date), 409 `ACCEPTANCE_NOT_EDITABLE`, 404, 422 `ACCEPTANCE_NO_CHANGES`. The issue route comes with 16H.2.
- **Database:** `0050_acceptance_protocols` — the table with its CHECKs (statuses, sequence ≥ 1, **ISSUED ⇒ time, snapshot and page present**), one draft per object, a number once per object; reversible, the downgrade **refuses while a protocol exists**. Checked on PostgreSQL 16: up → down → up, indexes and CHECKs as expected.
- **Tests:** backend `test_stage16h1_acceptance` 19 (the entries and each refusal by name and reason, remark change / removal and "a failed change changes nothing", the result of a surface and of the whole, FINAL vs PARTIAL, conditions, each blocker and the order, the absent customer's order of dates, the draft's life, the derived result from the real executions and DEFECT photos, a second room, foreign data, HTTP 401 / 404 / 409 / 422, the migration's chain, CHECKs, indexes, downgrade). **Mutation check:** 12 mutants of the rules (results, scope kind, notification order, blockers), all killed; one survivor (the acceptance on the day of the second call) got a test that pins the intended behaviour.
- **Full runs:** backend 5158 passed, 67 skipped, 1 known sandbox-root preflight failure (`test_stage14d2c_preflight`, fails identically without this change); `ruff` (F) on the new modules clean; the frontend is unchanged in this step (2193 passed at 16G.2).
- **Production:** not deployed (migrations `0039`–`0050` travel together).
- **Not in this step:** the document, the issue and the working version (16H.2); the phone screen (16H.3); the history of re-inspections; geometry and tolerances (the tolerance catalogue is empty — the owner's numbers pending); the warning about concealed works accepted late (no data link yet); the lead time of the notification (needs the Polish holiday calendar).
- **Next:** 16H.2 — only after the owner's "делаем 16H.2".

### Stage 16G.1 — the protocol of acceptance of concealed works: data, rules, document, issuing (2026-10-10, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; migration `0049_concealed_works`)
First step of 16G (owner: "Пуш и продолжаем"; split 16G.1 backend and document / 16G.2 the phone screen). Work that the next layers will **cover** (priming, glass fleece, mesh, repair of cracks, board joints, waterproofing ...) is accepted **before** it is covered, with photos as the evidence (contract § 13, annex 6).
- **Data (`concealed_works_protocols`):** one row per acceptance of one kind of work on one surface (`sequence` per object), the day and time, **the people present — or "the customer did not come" with the day he was notified** (contract § 13 ust. 3: a one-sided protocol with photos, the work goes on), the surface (room and surface names frozen at issue), the **kind of work from a new catalogue** (`concealed_work_kinds.json`: priming, glass fleece, reinforcing mesh, crack repair, board joints, waterproofing, other + a note), material and batch (contract § 11 ust. 4), **the evidence photos** chosen from the surface's photos of the category `HIDDEN_WORK` (Stage 14), the result (accepted / accepted with remarks) with remarks, the consent to cover (given / withheld). States `DRAFT` (one per object) → `ISSUED` (frozen) → `ARCHIVED`; nothing is deleted.
- **Rules (`domain/protocols/concealed.py`), deterministic:** every entry is checked by name and reason (the kind must be in the catalogue; the surface must be an active surface of the object; **a photo must be an active HIDDEN_WORK photo of that surface**; changing the surface drops the photos of the old one); blockers before issue, in the order of doing: executor profile, customer, an issued or signed contract, surface, kind of work (and a note for "other"), day, **people present or — when the customer is absent — the day of the notification**, **at least one photo** (without evidence nobody can say later what was covered), result (and remarks when "with remarks"), **consent to cover** (not asked of an absent customer).
- **The page (`concealed_works_document.py`, `concealed_works_protocol.html.j2`, version `1`, number prefix `ZANIK`):** the object, room, surface, kind of work, material, batch, the day and time, the contract (version and number); the people present, or the sentence about the absent customer and the day of the notification (pointing at § 13 ust. 3); the photos as a table (no., when taken, caption, a short reference to find the photo in the application); the result and remarks; the consent (or "not applicable — a one-sided protocol, the work goes on"); signatures. Photos are **listed, not embedded** (they stay in the application and in the photo report); embedding thumbnails is a possible later step.
- **Working version:** `POST /api/projects/{id}/documents/concealed-works/preview` — pale watermark, no number, no journal row, never refuses; follows the open draft or is a blank form with empty boxes, empty lines and five empty rows for the photos, to fill in on the spot before the work is covered.

### Stage 16F.3 — the protocol of handing over the premises on the phone (2026-10-10, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; no migration)
Last step of 16F (owner: "Пуш и делаем дальше"). The card "Protokół przekazania pomieszczeń" of the object, built for a contractor standing in the room: **minimum taps, large controls, every tap saved at once**. 16F is complete with this step.
- **Flow:** "Rozpocznij protokół przekazania" opens the draft (the same draft when one exists) and, when it has no day, **writes today** (editable); the card then shows the day and the time, the people present, the rooms, the meters and notes, the gate, and the buttons "Wersja robocza do wydruku (puste pola)", "Wystaw protokół", "Zwiń", "Odrzuć szkic" (a second tap to confirm). The working version can also be sent from the closed card.
- **People present:** a checkbox row (≥ 60 px) per active person of the register, plus "Inna osoba (imię i nazwisko, funkcja)" with "Dodaj osobę" / "Usuń" for somebody who is not in it; every change sends the whole list.
- **Rooms (one open at a time, so the screen stays short):** the header shows the room, "n z 14 wymagań" and the decision; inside — **"Wszystko spełnione" (one tap: every requirement met and the decision "Przekazane")**, then each requirement of the catalogue with the **number the contract asks for** ("Wymagane: 300 lx", "od 5 do 25 °C", "Tak"), four large state buttons in a 2×2 grid (Spełnione / Niespełnione / Warunkowo / Nie dotyczy, colour-coded, `aria-pressed`), a measured value (`inputMode="decimal"`; a range needs both limits, typed limits are remembered until both are there) and a note that appears for an unmet or conditional requirement; the existing damages; the decision as three buttons with the server's **suggestion** — "Przekazane" is **disabled** until every requirement is met, the stricter decisions are always available.
- **Saving:** each tap is one small `PATCH`; text and number fields save when the field is left (never per letter, and a blank over an empty field sends nothing); requests go **one at a time in the order of the taps**, the screen takes the server's answer (so the suggestion and the list of what is missing are always the server's), "Zapisuję…" shows while a request is in the air, and "Wersja robocza", "Wystaw" and "Odrzuć" wait for the saves in flight. A refused entry is named in words (PL / RU) by its reason.
- **Gate in words:** the server's blockers with room names ("Brakuje stanu wymagań: Salon (3).", "Brak decyzji dla: Łazienka.", "„Przekazane” przy niespełnionych wymaganiach: …"); "Wystaw protokół" is shut while any is left; a refusal of the server at issue replaces the list.
- **Backend:** one small change that the screen needs — an entry's **measured value and note can now be cleared** with an explicit `null` (before, only the whole entry could be removed, losing the state); a blank note counts as none.
- **Frontend files:** `components/ProjectHandover.tsx` (mounted after the contract card in `ProjectWorkspace`), `api/handovers.ts`, `previewHandoverPdf`, `types/handover.ts`, `utils/handover.ts`, PL / RU texts `handover.*`.

Second step of 16F (owner: "Пуш и Делаем 16F.2"). The data of 16F.1 become a numbered, frozen, sent document, plus a **working version with empty boxes and lines** to print and fill in by hand on the premises.
