### Stage 16F.1 — the protocol of handing over the premises: data, rules and API (2026-10-10, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; migration `0047_handover_protocols`)
First step of 16F (owner: "Пуш и делаем 16F"; split 16F.1 data and API / 16F.2 the document and the journal / 16F.3 the phone screen). The protocol records, **before the work starts, the state of each room against the requirements for the premises** (the same catalogue as annex 4 of the contract), who was present and what was decided. Nothing is invented: the numbers to meet are the contract's, the protocol only records what was found.
- **Data (`handover_protocols`):** one row per handover of one object (`sequence` per object — premises may be handed over in parts), `held_on` / `held_time`, `attendees` (persons of the register are **copied by name and role**, so a later change of the register never rewrites a protocol; an outsider is written by hand), `rooms` (per room: each requirement's state `YES / NO / CONDITIONAL / NOT_APPLICABLE` with an optional measured value and note, the existing damages, the decision), `meters`, `notes`. States `DRAFT` (at most one per object) → `ISSUED` (16F.2) → `ARCHIVED`; nothing is deleted.
- **Rules (`domain/protocols/handover.py`), deterministic:** the measured value must fit the kind of its requirement (a yes / no requirement has no number; a number or a range within bounds); the **suggested decision** of a room follows its findings (all met → handed over; an unmet one → not handed over; a conditional one → conditionally) and is `null` while a requirement is unanswered; **a room may be marked "handed over" only when every requirement is met or does not apply** — "conditionally" (the risk goes into the protocol, contract § 8 ust. 4 and § 17) or "not handed over" (§ 10) are always the owner's right; blockers before issue, in the order of doing: the day, the people present, at least one room, every requirement answered per room, a decision per room, no decision more favourable than the findings.
- **API:** `GET / POST /api/projects/{id}/handovers` (the list newest first; opening twice returns the same draft: 201 then 200), `GET / PATCH …/{hid}` (a partial change merged entry by entry; `null` clears), `POST …/{hid}/archive` (abandon a draft). The read model also carries `suggested`, `blockers`, the reference `contract` (the latest issued or signed one) and its `required_values` for the premises. Refusals: 422 `HANDOVER_INVALID` with the field and a reason (`WRONG_TYPE`, `NOT_AN_OPTION`, `TOO_LONG`, `BAD_TIME`, `UNKNOWN_ROOM`, `UNKNOWN_REQUIREMENT`, `UNKNOWN_PERSON`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`), 409 `HANDOVER_NOT_EDITABLE`, 404 for a foreign project, protocol, room or person; nothing is applied when one change is refused.
- **Database:** `0047_handover_protocols`, reversible; the downgrade **refuses while any protocol exists** (evidence). Checked on PostgreSQL 16: a second draft, a repeated sequence and an unknown status are refused by the database; the downgrade refuses with a protocol present, then drops the table and the upgrade restores it.
- **Tests:** backend `test_stage16f1_handover` 26 (the day / time / texts, attendees, per-room requirements with merge and clearing, 11 wrong-entry cases by name and reason, a foreign room changes nothing, the suggested decision and the "handed over only when met" rule, the blockers, the draft's life, foreign data, the contract's requirements, HTTP, the migration). **Mutation check:** 12 mutants of the rules and the service, all killed (three survivors found first got tests).
- **Full run:** backend 5106 passed, 67 skipped, 1 known sandbox-root preflight failure (fails identically without this change); no frontend change in this step.
- **Production:** not deployed (migrations `0039`–`0047` travel together).

### Stage 16E.4 — signing: the issued contract becomes SIGNED and its estimate ACCEPTED; closing (2026-10-10, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; migration `0046_contract_signed`)
Last step of 16E. The contract is signed **on paper** (no electronic signature, plan 16A); the application only records the fact, the day written under the signatures and what it changes.
- **Sign:** `POST /api/projects/{id}/contracts/{cid}/sign` with `{"signed_on": "YYYY-MM-DD"}` → the contract goes `ISSUED → SIGNED` and **the estimate that priced it goes `FINAL → ACCEPTED`, in one transaction**; the frozen conditions, snapshot and page are untouched. Refusals are 422 `CONTRACT_SIGN_REFUSED` with a reason the screen has a sentence for: `SIGNED_ON_IN_FUTURE`, `SIGNED_ON_BEFORE_ISSUE` (a day before the contract was issued), `ESTIMATE_CHANGED` (the estimate is gone, archived or back to a draft), `ALREADY_SIGNED` (another contract of the object is signed; also guaranteed by the database against two simultaneous requests). A contract that is not issued is 409 `CONTRACT_NOT_EDITABLE`; a foreign project / contract is 404.
- **Close:** `POST …/{cid}/close` takes an `ISSUED` contract (the customer did not sign) or a `SIGNED` one (it ended) to the archive; the estimate stays as it is (an accepted estimate remains accepted). A draft is abandoned through the old route, not closed.
- **`ContractRead`** now also carries `issued_at`, `estimate_version` and `signed_on`.
- **Database:** `0046_contract_signed` adds `contracts.signed_on` (date), the CHECK `ck_contracts_signed_has_date` (SIGNED ⇒ a day) and the partial unique index `uq_contracts_one_signed` (at most one SIGNED contract per object). Reversible; the downgrade **refuses while any contract carries a day of signing** (even an archived one: the date of a signature is evidence). Checked on PostgreSQL 16: upgrade, a second SIGNED refused by the index, SIGNED without a day refused by the CHECK, downgrade refused with a signing day present, then downgrade and upgrade again.
- **Frontend:** in the contract card, an issued contract shows the block "Data podpisania" (a date field, today by default, not later than today) and the button "Umowa podpisana" with a second tap to confirm (changing the date withdraws the confirmation); a signed one shows the day and the accepted estimate version; both offer "Zamknij umowę" / "Zakończ umowę (do archiwum)" with a second tap; the server's refusals are said in words (PL / RU).
- **Tests:** backend `test_stage16e4_signing` 13 (the one-step change, states, the day rules, a changed estimate, one signed contract per object, close, foreign project, HTTP, the migration's chain / rules / downgrade); frontend 9 new (touch-sized date and button, the second tap, the four refusals, closing, signed / draft / archived states, RU). **Mutation check:** 8 mutants of the service, 7 killed; the survivor (the owner / project scope of the estimate lookup) is a defence in depth with no observable difference for a consistent database.
- **Mobile check (Chromium, 320 / 390 / 412 px, PL / RU, issued and signed states):** no horizontal overflow, every control ≥ 44 px.
- **Full runs:** backend 5075 passed + the 5 head-pin / schema tests that the full run caught (they pinned `0045` as the head; updated and rerun green), 67 skipped, 1 known sandbox-root preflight failure (fails identically without this change); frontend 2154 passed, `tsc` clean, `vite build` OK.
- **Production:** not deployed (migrations `0039`–`0046` travel together).
- **Not in this step:** the handover protocol (16F), the concealed works protocol (16G), the final acceptance (16H), the protective documents (16I).
- **Next:** 16F — the handover of the premises (protocol) — only after the owner's "делаем 16F".

### Stage 16E.3 — the clause catalogue: the prototype contract of the owner in the application (2026-10-10, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; no migration)
Third step of 16E (owner: "берем за основу этот документ и вводим его к нам в приложение"). The prototype contract (23 sections + annexes, researched against similar Polish contracts, the Civil Code and the consumer-rights act) became **data**: `contracts/catalog/clauses.json` version 2, 112 numbered clauses and annexes 6–12. Nothing is written by the code; the wording is the owner's and waits for the lawyer.
- **Mechanisms (`contracts/clauses.py`, `contracts/clause_render.py`):** a **placeholder** `{name}` is replaced by a value of the contract (price, VAT and gross computed from the owner's VAT rate, advance amount, dates, answers, the executor's and the customer's contacts) — an unknown value is **an empty line to write in**, never a guess; a clause has **variants** with conditions (`consumer`, `!partial_acceptance`, `penalty_per_day` …) over a **three-valued** fact (true / false / not answered): when the deciding answer is missing, every possible variant is printed with a box ☐ to tick by hand (the working version can be talked through with the customer); a clause keeps its **number** whatever its variant (references like "§ 10 ust. 5" are always right; an optional clause may only be the last of its section); § 20 (consumer's withdrawal) and annex 11 print only for a consumer (or an entrepreneur with consumer rights) outside the executor's premises, otherwise § 20 stays with the line "Nie dotyczy"; Polish forms of "dnia / dni", "Dnia roboczego / Dni roboczych", "miesiąca / miesięcy".
- **Questions to the lawyer** (`review_notes` L2, L3, L4, L5, L7, L8, L13, L14, L15) are part of the catalogue, **never printed** in a client document, and the catalogue **cannot be `approved` while one is open**; until approval every contract carries the strong "WERSJA ROBOCZA" watermark.
- **Catalogue guards:** every `§ n ust. m` reference must point to an existing clause (a Civil Code "art. 355 § 2" is not a reference), unknown placeholders / conditions / stray braces are refused, numbering must be 1, 2, 3 …, the sections are exactly the 23 keys of the contract template (version 2), the annexes exactly 6–12. One reference of the prototype was wrong (§ 6 ust. 3 pointed to § 15 instead of § 14 ust. 4) and was corrected.
- **Questionnaire v2 (31 questions, was 17):** new REQUIRED `client_status`, `conclusion_mode`; OPEN `paid_orders_persons`, `work_hours`, `vat_rate_percent`, `price_validity_days`, `payment_account`, `materials_supplier`, `contractor_representative`, `insurance_sum`, `insurance_policy`, `penalty_mode`, `penalty_rate_per_day`, `penalty_cap_percent`, `downtime_days_limit` (no default, by the owner's decision: left open, a line to write in); `contractual_penalty` (free text) replaced by the three penalty questions; new groups "Cena" and "Wykonanie prac"; PL / RU labels, hints and choices.
- **The document:** header with the two boxes (customer status, way of concluding), § 1 … § 23 with the clauses, the table of authorised persons (with the column "Zlecenia płatne") after § 21 ust. 2, **signatures right after § 23**, then annexes 1–5 (card, plan, estimate, requirements, regulation: as before) and annexes 6–12 from the catalogue (forms of the protocols and notices as lists of lines to complete, the consumer information with the statutory withdrawal form, the RODO clause). Blank values inside a paragraph are short inline lines.
- **Frontend:** only the catalogue-driven questionnaire grew (the screen draws every question of the server catalogue); `QuestionGroup` type, PL / RU texts; tests updated for six required answers.
- **Tests:** backend `test_stage16e3_clauses` 25 (values and Polish forms, gross / advance with half-up rounding, three-valued facts, choice of variants, optional clause and stable numbers over 1 296 answer combinations, consumer section / annex 11, references, broken text, conditional clause in the middle, approval with open notes, negated condition); `test_stage16e2_contract`, `test_stage16e1_contract_answers`, `test_stage16b3_catalog` updated. **Mutation check:** 11 mutants of the render / validation code, all killed (three survivors found first — negation, rounding, the Civil Code reference — got tests).
- **Visual check:** the full contract with an off-premises consumer (21 pages) and a blank working version (23 pages) were rendered to PDF and looked at (first page, §§ 5–7, 19–23 with the signatures, annex 11); found and fixed: blanks inside a paragraph were full-width lines.
- **Mobile check (Chromium, 320 / 390 / 412 px, PL / RU, 48 controls):** no horizontal overflow, every control ≥ 44 px.
- **Full runs:** backend 5067 passed, 67 skipped, 1 failed (the known sandbox-root preflight test `test_workspace_preflight_passes_with_private_mounts_and_valid_passfile`, failing identically without this change); frontend 2145 passed, `tsc` clean, `vite build` OK.
- **Production:** not deployed (migrations `0039`–`0045` travel together; this step adds none).
- **Owner's decision (2026-10-10):** the lawyer's review is postponed ("пока без юриста"): the catalogue stays an unapproved draft with the watermark; the downtime threshold stays open for the questionnaire.
- **Not in this step:** the lawyer's review and the owner's numbers (tolerances, class criteria) — then `approved` can be set; the transition to SIGNED and archiving a signed contract (16E.4).
- **Next:** 16E.4 — `SIGNED` (the estimate becomes `ACCEPTED`) and the archive of the signed contract.

### Stage 16E.2 — the contract: the gate, the frozen snapshot, the document with annexes and a printable working version (2026-10-10, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; migration `0045_contract_issue`)
Second step of 16E. The contract is made of **data, never prose written by the code**: the answers of the questionnaire (16E.1), the persons who may accept the work, the price of the current estimate (**without VAT**) and, as annexes of the same issue, the technological card, the production plan, the requirements for the premises and the regulation of acceptance. The **wording** of the clauses is a server catalogue the owner and a lawyer approve (16E.3): until then every section prints "— do uzupełnienia —" and every issued contract carries the strong "WERSJA ROBOCZA" watermark.
- **The gate (`domain/contracts/gate.py`)** — deterministic, one list of what to fix, in the order of fixing: executor profile; a client with an address (street, postal code, city — 16B.1); every REQUIRED answer; the chosen persons still active and authorised; at least one surface with planned works and each of them with its agreed standard and a finished inspection (the rule of the numbered card); an estimate that exists and is FINAL (or ACCEPTED). `GET /api/projects/{id}/contracts/{cid}/gate` → `{ready, blockers:[{code, details}]}`.
- **Issue:** `POST …/contracts/{cid}/issue` → 202 + journal row `UMOWA/…` (a refusal is 422 `CONTRACT_GATE_BLOCKED` with the list and **takes no number**; a contract that is no longer a draft is 409). The draft is **frozen**: `issued_at`, the `snapshot` (answers with defaults, the chosen persons, the client and address, the executor, the estimate id / version / total, the clause catalogue version and approval, the scope counts), the **exact page** (`document_html`) and the estimate that priced it; an earlier issued version of the object is superseded (ARCHIVED). **The PDF of an issued contract is always made from the frozen page, never from live data** (a test changes the object's name and the person's name after issue and the re-made PDF still says the old ones). A new version starts from the last version's answers.
- **The document:** header, parties (the customer with address), date and place, ten numbered sections (subject, scope, price, schedule, payments, acceptance, downtime, warranty, penalty, final provisions) each with its data rows and the clause paragraphs (empty now), the list of authorised persons, and **Annexes 1–5** — the technological card and the production plan **embedded** (the same body partials as their own documents), the estimate reference (version and net total), the requirements for the premises with the owner's values (a requirement without a value is an empty line), the regulation of acceptance (the standards of the classes in scope with their lighting conditions, the defect classes with their outcomes and "criteria: do uzupełnienia", the instruments, the tolerances — "do uzupełnienia" while the catalogue is empty; S1–S4 / Q1–Q4 stay finish standards, not geometry).
- **Working version with empty lines:** `POST …/documents/contract/preview` → the whole packet (contract + annexes) with a pale watermark, no number, no journal row; it follows the open draft or is a blank form, and **never refuses**. The owner prints it and talks it through with the customer.
- **Clause catalogue:** `clauses.json` (version, `approved`, `approved_by`, `approved_on`, ten sections with Polish titles and empty paragraphs); the model refuses an incomplete approval, an approved catalogue without wording and any other set of sections.
- **Database:** `0045_contract_issue` adds `issued_at`, `snapshot`, `document_html`, `estimate_id`, `estimate_version` to `contracts` and the rule **`ISSUED` / `SIGNED` ⇒ time, snapshot and page present** (CHECK `ck_contracts_frozen_when_issued`); widens `ck_issued_documents_kind` with `CONTRACT`; reversible, the downgrade **refuses** while an issued / signed contract or a contract journal row exists. Checked on native PostgreSQL 16: the freeze CHECK refuses an issued contract without time, snapshot or page and accepts drafts, abandoned drafts and complete ones; the kind CHECK text; the refusal with one issued contract and one journal row (head stays); down after the deletion and up again; `test_stage15f1_postgres` + `test_stage15c_postgres` 5 passed.
- **Found by the full run:** `POST /documents` with `{"kind":"CONTRACT"}` was accepted by the general request and would have issued a **photo report** — the general request no longer admits `CONTRACT` (a contract has its own route), a test pins it.
- **Frontend:** the questionnaire card gets the block "Gotowość umowy" / "Готовность договора" (the blockers in words in PL / RU: the missing questions by name, the client address fields, the surfaces and what each lacks, the estimate's state), the buttons "Wersja robocza do wydruku (puste pola)", "Wystaw umowę" (enabled only when the gate is open; the server's list is shown if it still refuses) and, after an issue, "Nowa wersja umowy"; the journal names the row "Umowa"; the gate is read again after every save.
- **Tests:** backend `test_stage16e2_contract` 32 (the gate alone and together, the document's data and annexes, the strong watermark while unapproved and none for an approved catalogue (patched), the real PDF with the number on every page, the working version and blank packet, the regulation's classes, the clause catalogue's refusals, issue / freeze / journal / delivery, a blocked contract takes no number, no second issue or edit, a new version supersedes the old one, the frozen page, preview, HTTP, migration); the nine head pins now expect `0045_contract_issue`; skeleton tests now use the handover protocol (the contract has its own template); frontend `ProjectContract.test` 21, `contracts.test` 3, `documents.test` 7; full frontend 2145 passed, `tsc` clean, `vite build` OK. Mutation checks (10): the estimate state ignored, the authority ignored, an older issue not superseded, a new version without the answers, unapproved wording not a draft, the page not frozen, a re-make from live data, the price dropped, the gate skipped, the owner filter dropped — all caught.
- **Backend full run:** 5041 passed, 67 skipped, 1 deselected (the known sandbox-root preflight test).
- **Visual check:** the issued contract and the working version were rendered to PDF (7 and 9 pages) and looked at (the first page, an annex); corrections made after looking (the object's address on one line, the doubled full stop in the regulation).
- **Mobile check (Chromium, 320 / 390 / 412 px, PL / RU, the whole form with five long blockers):** no horizontal overflow, all 35 controls ≥ 44 px, the blockers wrap.
- **Production:** not deployed (migrations `0039`–`0045` travel together with the other Stage 16 sub-stages).
- **Not in this step (16E.3):** the wording of the clauses and its approval, the transition to SIGNED (the estimate becomes ACCEPTED) and archiving a signed contract.
- **Next:** 16E.3 — the clause catalogue (wording written by the owner, version, approval) and SIGNED.

### Stage 16E.1 — the contract of an object and the questionnaire "Составить договор" (2026-10-09, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; migration `0044_contracts`)
First step of 16E (owner: "делаем", with the split 16E.1 questionnaire and data / 16E.2 contract and the gate / 16E.3 clause catalogue and approval). Everything the contract will say as a number, a date or a person is an **answer of the owner** here — the questions, their kinds, which are required and the only two defaults come from the server catalogue (16B.3).
- **Database:** `0044_contracts` — table `contracts` (`owner_id`, `project_id` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`; `version`, `status` DRAFT / ISSUED / SIGNED / ARCHIVED, `answers` JSON, `questionnaire_version`; CHECKs on the status and `version >= 1`; unique `(project_id, version)`; a **partial unique index allows one draft per object**; index `(project_id, status)`); reversible. Checked on native PostgreSQL 16: the partial index (`WHERE status = 'DRAFT'`) refuses a second draft and lets an abandoned draft make room, a version twice, an unknown state and version 0 are refused, deleting an object takes its contracts, down / up clean.
- **Backend:** `domain/contracts/answers.py` — what an answer may be by the kind of its question, all in one stored form: trimmed text (≤ 500, blank = no answer), an ISO date, whole numbers in a range (percent 0–100, days 0–365, months 0–120, count 0–100; a bool or a string is not a number), money as `"150.50"` (comma accepted, at most two places, never negative), a choice from the catalogue's options, a list of persons without repeats (**only active persons of this object who are marked "may accept the work and sign the protocols"**, else `UNKNOWN_PERSON` / `NOT_AUTHORISED`), the values of the premises requirements by their kind (yes/no, a number, a range with `min <= max`; unknown requirement refused); the end date may not be before the start (also when only one is sent); nothing is applied when one change of several is refused; `null` / blank / empty list clears an answer. `effective_answers` = stored + the two accepted defaults (appearance 3 working days, partial acceptance yes); `missing_required` lists the REQUIRED questions without an answer. `ContractService` (owner-scoped), routes `GET / POST /api/projects/{id}/contracts` (POST opens the draft: 201 when new, 200 with the same draft), `GET …/{id}`, `PATCH …/{id}/answers` (only a draft: 409 `CONTRACT_NOT_EDITABLE` otherwise; 422 `CONTRACT_ANSWER_INVALID` with `{key, reason}`), `POST …/{id}/archive` (abandon a draft; the next draft is the next version).
- **Frontend:** card "Umowa" / "Договор" on the object screen (after the adjacent works): "Skomponuj umowę" / "Продолжить черновик", then the whole questionnaire drawn from the catalogue — groups, required / optional marks, hints, inputs by kind (date picker, numeric and decimal keyboards, selects, a checklist of authorised persons with a hint when there are none, the premises requirements with yes/no, number and range fields), progress of the required answers and the list of what is missing, save sends **only what changed** (an emptied field is `null`), a refused answer is named by its question and reason in the language of the interface, "abandon the draft" after a second tap; PL / RU; every control ≥ 44 px.
- **Tests:** backend `test_stage16e1_contract_answers` 51 (every kind with a good and many bad answers, atomic refusal, clearing, date order, the two defaults only, required list, migration chain / shape / the database's own rules / cascade, the API: open once, partial saves and completeness, 422 shape, authorised persons only, abandon and the next version, owner and object isolation, tokens, every reason has a PL and RU sentence); the nine head pins now expect `0044_contracts`; frontend `ProjectContract.test` 13 (draws every question and requirement of the **real server catalogue** in PL and RU, defaults, authorised persons, only changed values sent with typed values, null clearing, requirement values by kind, a refused answer named, continue a draft, abandon after a second tap, retry), full 2133 passed, `tsc` clean, `vite build` OK. Mutation checks (7): a bool accepted as a number, the authority not checked, the date order dropped, an invented default, a non-draft editable, the owner filter dropped, a default not counted as an answer — all caught.
- **Backend full run:** 5011 passed, 67 skipped, 1 deselected (the known sandbox-root preflight test).
- **Mobile check (Chromium, 320 / 390 / 412 px, PL / RU, the whole questionnaire open with a long person name and role):** no horizontal overflow, all 33 controls ≥ 44 px, long labels wrap; page height 3.5–4 screens.
- **Hint corrected:** the PL / RU hint of "who accepts" now says "persons authorised to accept the work and sign the protocols" (the rule the server enforces).
- **Production:** not deployed (migrations `0039`–`0044` travel together with the other Stage 16 sub-stages).

### Stage 16C — the technological card, with a printable working version with empty fields (2026-10-09, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; migration `0041_issued_documents_tech_card`)
First document of the chain "technological card → production plan → estimate → contract" (owner: "принимаю рекомендации, делаем 16C" + "необходимо, чтобы была возможность скачать версию рабочую с пустыми полями … чтобы можно было распечатать и проговорить с заказчиком").
- **The document (`Karta technologiczna`)** — per room and surface: the substrate, the agreed finishing standard (S1–S4 / Q1–Q4 with its short name from the documented definitions, no millimetre), the inspection (date, answered checklist, risks with the "work is to be stopped" note, notes), and the planned works **in order** with unit, quantity (from the current estimate by the work's stable occurrence key; empty when it is not in an estimate) and the **technological break after each work**. No prices, no clause. The canonical names "Wall 1 / Floor / Ceiling" are printed in Polish.
- **Two forms of one builder (`tech_card_document.py`)**: **numbered** (`KART/…`, journal, no watermark; refused with `TECH_CARD_EMPTY` / `TECH_CARD_INCOMPLETE` — the answer lists every surface with works that lacks the agreed standard or a finished inspection — and `EXECUTOR_PROFILE_REQUIRED`), and the **working version** (watermark "WERSJA ROBOCZA", no number, no journal row, executor profile not needed): it never refuses; everything missing prints as an **empty line to write in by hand**, every surface gets a table with four free numbered rows (the works it already has fill them first), a free box for the inspection result and for remarks; an object with no rooms yet gets a blank room with three blank surfaces. Meant to be printed before the inspection and talked through with the customer.
- **Delivery** as in Stage 15: PDF to the owner's chat with the bot (`POST /api/projects/{id}/documents` with `{"kind":"TECH_CARD"}` → 202 + journal row; `POST /api/projects/{id}/documents/tech-card/preview` → the working version, 200). The Mini App cannot offer a file save dialog, so "download" is the chat file, exactly like the estimate preview.
- **Database:** `0041_issued_documents_tech_card` widens `ck_issued_documents_kind` to `('ESTIMATE','PHOTO_REPORT','TECH_CARD')`; reversible, and the downgrade **refuses** (does not delete) while a card is in the journal. ### Stage 16B.3 — catalogues of the contract and the protocols, without legal text (2026-10-09, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; no migration)
Third and last step of 16B (plan v3, owner answers Q9–Q14). Server data that the contract questionnaire (16E), the handover protocol (16F) and the acceptance (16H) will draw; **no clause, no norm, no number**.
- **Package `app/domain/contracts/`** — `catalog.py` (strict Pydantic models, `extra="forbid"`, frozen; the loader refuses a wrong file: duplicate keys, a label key off the convention `contractCatalog.<section>.<key>`, a quality class missing from the evaluation catalogue, a tolerance with an unknown instrument) and six JSON files:
  - `premises_requirements.json` — 14 requirements in 7 groups (lighting, windows and openings, temperature and humidity, utilities, access, cleanliness and protection, substrate), each yes/no or a number with a unit and **never a value**: the numbers are answers of the owner;
  - `assessment_instruments.json` — 8 instruments (2 m straightedge, feeler gauge, spirit level, laser level, tape or laser distance meter, moisture meter, raking-light lamp, adhesion test) with what each measures;
  - `evaluation_conditions.json` — the eight classes S1–S4 / Q1–Q4 with the lighting kind taken from the documented definitions (S2 diffuse, S4 **agreed before the work**, Q4 raking light) and **no millimetre** (Stage 12 §27.1: S/Q are finish standards, geometry is separate);
  - `defect_classes.json` — removable (→ accepted with remarks) and significant (→ not accepted); `criteria_pl` is null: the criteria are the owner's and the lawyer's to approve;
  - `tolerances.json` — **the format only, empty**: a tolerance without a source (`norm_ref`), a positive limit, known instruments and known classes is refused, so no guessed number can enter;
  - `questionnaire.json` — the 17 questions of "compose the contract" (who may accept and sign — required, from the register of persons; dates and place; advance, payment mode and term; warranty; contractual penalty; **downtime rate per day (open, may stay "......")** and its cap; customer's appearance term (default 3 working days, the owner's recommendation); partial acceptances (default yes); re-inspection limit; notice of the premises' readiness; the values of the premises requirements), each REQUIRED or OPEN, with its kind, unit, options and defaults — the only defaults are the two recommendations the owner accepted.
- **API:** `GET /api/contract-catalog` (signed-in owner, static content) serves all six; the frontend has the types, `fetchContractCatalog` and the PL / RU interface texts of every label and hint (`contractCatalog.*` in `pl.json` / `ru.json`; the Polish document wording lives in the catalogues as `text_pl`).

Second step of 16B (owner decision Q10: a contract item "who may accept the work and sign the protocols", one person or a list, concrete persons). A register of persons per object; the contract and the protocols (later sub-stages) copy the chosen persons into their own snapshot, so a later change never rewrites an issued document.

Checked on native PostgreSQL 16: both CHECKs refuse bad rows, deleting an object takes its persons with it, down / up are clean, no `alembic check` drift for the table.

- **Tests:** backend `test_stage16b2_representatives` 16 (migration chain and shape, the database refuses a wrong side and an empty name, the project takes its persons with it, normalization, defaults, six wrong inputs, order and archived, partial PATCH and null, owner isolation, a person is not reachable through another object); the seven head-pin tests now expect `0040_project_representatives`; frontend `ProjectRepresentatives.test` 10, full 2091 passed, `tsc` clean, `vite build` OK. ### Stage 15H.2 — one work asked for by several defects: wall and reason on the card, a warning and a confirmation (2026-10-09, DEPLOYED to production and ACCEPTED by the owner; no migration)
Found by the owner on the production check of 15H.1: the same work is suggested for different defects, the cards look like duplicates (the card shows neither the wall nor the defect), and "Dodaj do prac" appends the work to the wall's plan every time, so the estimate holds it several times. Owner decision (2026-10-09): variant A of A / B / C — show the context and warn, keep the Stage 10 rule "duplicates are allowed" (two coats are legitimate).
- **Facts (code):** a recommendation row is one per (inspection, trigger, source, work), so two defects asking for the same work give two cards; `append_one_planned_work_no_commit` never checks whether the price item is already in the plan (by design); the 15E.3 report already merges per (wall, work), the estimate does not.
- **Backend (read-only, no migration):** `WorkRecommendationService.describe_context` — for each card: the wall (`surface_name`, `surface_type`), the defect (`reason_key`: the title key of the risk, else the label key of the finding), `in_plan_count` (how many times the work — the accepted snapshot item, else the current price item — is already in that wall's plan) and `same_work_other_cards` (other live, non-dismissed cards of the same wall asking for the same work). Up to 5 queries per list whatever the number of cards; attached in the list, evaluate, dismiss, reconsider and accept answers (the accept answer used its own price-item path and needed an explicit attach — found by the HTTP test).
- **Frontend:** the card shows "Powierzchnia: …" (generated names localized: "Ściana 1" / "Стена 1", "Sufit" / "Потолок") and "Powód: …" in the interface language; an amber note "already in the plan of this surface (N×)" or "another card asks for the same work"; adding a work that is already in the wall's plan first asks "Dodać tę pracę jeszcze raz?" (inline, full-width buttons ≥ 44 px, no `window.confirm`); after an add the list is read again so the other cards learn about it. A card without duplicate facts behaves as before.
- **Tests:** backend `test_stage15h2_recommendation_context` 7 (wall and defect, two defects one work, dismissed card not counted, work in the plan counted incl. second add = 2 occurrences, another wall not counted, fixed query count and read-only, HTTP answers); the existing 122 recommendation tests and 30 of 15E.3 unchanged; frontend `RecommendationPanel.test` 54 (+6; test B adapted: the list is read again after an accept), full 2074 passed, `tsc` clean, `vite build` OK. Mutation checks (7): in-plan count always 0, dismissed counted as another card, other wall counted, accept answer without context, no confirmation, no refresh after accept, surface name not localized — all caught.
- **Backend full run:** 4844 passed, 67 skipped, 1 deselected (the known sandbox-root preflight test); the one-off render-worker SIGSEGV of the earlier 15H.1 run did not repeat.
- **Mobile check (Chromium, 320 / 390 / 412 px, PL / RU, light / dark, 12 cases with the confirmation open):** no horizontal overflow, buttons of the confirmation ≥ 44 px, texts wrap.
- **Production:** deployed 2026-10-09 by `docs/STAGE_15H2_PRODUCTION_RUNBOOK_RU.md` (A0–A6, owner-run, every step with its own "да"; no migration; commit `2b9543a`, rollback tags `:pre-15h2`, menu button `?v=2b9543a`). Owner checked A6 on the phone: all 7 points PASS (wall and defect on every card in the interface language, the "same work asked by another card" note, the "already in the plan (N×)" note after the first add, the "Dodać jeszcze raz?" confirmation with Anuluj, Odrzuć, a card without a duplicate as before, 320–412 px PL/RU).

### Stage 15H.1 — blocked photo report: clear reasons and links to the fix (2026-10-09, DEPLOYED to production and checked by the owner; no migration)
Found by the owner during the 15H phone walkthrough (A8) on production (backend `aad9e67`): the estimate PDF was sent (`KOSZ/2026/10/09/0118`, 1 page, journal row correct), but the photo report refused with "Brak ceny w kosztorysie" and the screen did not say what to do. Owner remarks: (1) the listed works must be clickable and lead to the place with the problem; (2) after dismissing a recommendation the warning disappeared, but after adding one to the works ("Dodaj do prac") it stayed; (3) the warning must be readable and in the interface language; (4) the report was not sent; the over-60-photos flow was not checked (the object has 4 photos).
- **Cause of (2)/(4), not a defect of accepting:** by the Stage 11 contract accepting a recommendation only appends the work to the surface's plan and **never touches an estimate**; the price is read from the current estimate, so an accepted work has no line there until the estimate is updated (a DRAFT: "Aktualizuj kosztorys") or a new version is created (a FINAL one: "Utwórz nową wersję"). The old hint ("trafi do kosztorysu") promised the opposite.
- **Backend (additive, no migration):** `RecommendedWork` gains `block_reason` (PENDING → NO_ESTIMATE → NOT_IN_ESTIMATE → NO_PRICE, in the order the owner has to act), `surface_type`, `inspection_id`, `inspection_surface_id`, `inspection_plane`; `RecommendedWorks.estimate_id`; the photo-report summary returns `unpriced_items` (structured: raw names, reason, ids of the room / surface / inspection), `estimate_id`, `estimate_status`. `unpriced_works` (text list) stays, the server refusal `RECOMMENDED_WORK_UNPRICED` is unchanged.
- **Frontend:** each blocked work is a full-width card-button (≥ 44 px): the work name and the surface name in the **interface language** (price-book keys and generated "Wall 1" / "Ceiling" go through the locale dictionaries), the place, one sentence of what to do for its reason (a settled estimate says "create a new version", a draft says "update the estimate"), and the action line. A tap opens the **inspection** that holds the recommendation (room → inspection list → inspection; Back returns step by step) or the **current estimate** (the list of estimates when the object has none). The documents card remembers that it was open (`sessionStorage`, per object) so it is open again when the owner comes back. New texts in `documents.*` (PL/RU), the `RECOMMENDED_WORK_UNPRICED` sentence now also says to bring the accepted work into the estimate.
- **Tests:** backend `test_stage15e3_recommended_works` 30 (+4: reasons, dismissed vs accepted, summary leads to the inspection and the estimate, no estimate), `test_stage15f2_api` extended; frontend `ProjectDocuments.test` 19 (+5), `ProjectWorkspace.test` 46 (+2: leads to the inspection / to the estimate), `unpricedTarget.test` 1; frontend full 2068 passed (94 files), `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` OK. Mutation checks: pending → estimate, draft/final sentences swapped, surface name not localized, estimate id dropped (all caught); the plane-target mutation first survived and led to the extraction of `inspectionTargetOf` with its own test (now caught).
- **Backend full run:** 4837 passed, 67 skipped, 1 deselected (the known sandbox-root `test_stage14d2c_preflight` failure, also red on the untouched tree). **Observation:** one earlier full run failed `test_stage15b_renderer::test_a_cancelled_render_kills_its_process_and_frees_the_slot` — the render worker died with SIGSEGV (exit -11; `dmesg`: one segfault of `python3.12`, instruction-fetch fault). Not reproducible: 25 runs of that test, 60 sequential renders and 120 cancel-then-render cycles in 3 parallel processes without a failure, and the immediately repeated full run was clean; the renderer and worker were not touched by 15H.1. - **15F.1 (commit `90eb91f`) — journal and numbering.** Table `issued_documents` + reversible migration `0038_issued_documents` (kind / status CHECKs, unique `(owner, number)` and `(owner, project, project_seq)`, cascade with the user and the project, no file); `IssuedDocumentService`: numbers are given when an attempt starts, under a lock on the **owner's** row; a second tap on the same running document returns the same row; a PENDING attempt older than 15 minutes is FAILED / INTERRUPTED; owner-scoped reads. **PostgreSQL found a real design error:** a lock on the project row was not enough because the number is unique per owner (two objects of one owner issued at the same moment took the same number); the lock moved to the owner's row; without it all three race tests fail.
- **15F.2 — issuing and delivery.** `DocumentIssuer`: everything cheap is checked in the request (owner, estimate FINAL / ACCEPTED, executor profile, photo limit) and answered at once; the slow part (render + send) is a background task with its own session, one render at a time, at most 3 queued (`DOCUMENT_QUEUE_FULL` before a number is taken), every end recorded (SENT or FAILED with a stable code; unexpected errors logged and recorded as INTERNAL_ERROR; a cancelled run is INTERRUPTED). `TelegramBotApiDelivery` (`sendDocument` with the backend's token): 403 / "chat not found" → TELEGRAM_CHAT_UNAVAILABLE (the owner must press Start in the bot), 429 / 5xx / network → TELEGRAM_UNAVAILABLE, other 4xx → TELEGRAM_REJECTED, switched off → DELIVERY_DISABLED; **the token never reaches a log, an error text or a traceback** (HTTP client loggers raised to WARNING, no chained exceptions, no `raise_for_status`). API: `POST /api/projects/{p}/documents` (202), `GET` journal and one document (polling), `GET .../photo-report/summary` (counts per room and the limit, no photo is read), `POST .../estimates/{e}/preview-pdf` (a draft with the watermark, no number, not journaled). The running number is printed in the header ("Nr kolejny dokumentu dla obiektu"); a part of a photo report is journaled with its rooms.
- **15F.3 — screens.** "Wyślij PDF" / "Podgląd PDF (wersja robocza)" in the estimate summary; card "Dokumenty PDF" in the object (closed by default, loads nothing until opened): photo report summary, the choice of rooms when it is over the 60-photo limit (live total, general photos on request), the journal "Wysłane dokumenty" (kind, number, running number, date, pages, size, status; a failed one with its reason; a running one is followed). Texts come from stable codes (`documents.errors`, PL / RU); a backend test fails when a code has no sentence in either language.

### Stage 14J — adversarial / full verification of Stage 14 (2026-10-08, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not deployed; tests, one model fix, no migration)

Owner started 14J on 2026-10-08. Plan: `docs/STAGE_14J_VERIFICATION_PLAN_RU.md`. No new features; the gates of architecture §19 were run and what they found was fixed.
- **14J.1 — PostgreSQL 16 (native, disposable loopback cluster under `/var/tmp`, database `pe_scratch_test_14j`, removed afterwards; no Docker).** `alembic upgrade head` from an empty database → `0036_photo_annotation_outline`; `downgrade` to `0030_surface_work_executions` and `upgrade` again, both directions clean; `alembic check` shows **no drift for the photo tables** (`photo_assets`, `photo_attachments`, `photo_annotations`) — the only notes are column comments and the old `communication_*` tables, outside Stage 14. The existing opt-in PostgreSQL modules pass: 14C.6B guard + concurrency, 14D.2A snapshot / `pg_dump` (run through a throw-away `docker exec` shim that executes `psql` / `pg_dump` natively against the scratch cluster), 14D.5 drill tool — **73 passed**.
- **14J.2 — new PostgreSQL proof for 14F–14I (`tests/test_stage14j_postgres.py`, opt-in, 8 tests, 20 race rounds):** marker coordinate and position CHECKs (and the 0 / 1 boundaries), the CHECK of every attachment context (INSPECTION / FINDING / WORK / ROOM with a wrong target column), the partial unique indexes of active INSPECTION (with and without a question) / FINDING / WORK attachments and the archived-duplicate exception, the cascade attachment → markers; **limit of 10 markers under concurrency** (9 existing + 12 contenders → exactly one wins; 25 contenders from empty → exactly 10, positions 0..9 without gaps; with the row lock removed 4 creates got through where one was allowed, so the proof is real); concurrent contour rewrites (one valid contour, never a mixture) and concurrent deletes; counts and the 14I read model on 27 and 540 photos — exact against the inserted truth, **19 SELECTs in both cases** (does not grow), counts 84 ms and report 113 ms for 540 photos, times UTC-aware.
- **Defect found and fixed (14J-1):** on PostgreSQL a cleared contour (`PATCH outline: null`) was stored as the JSON document `null`, not SQL `NULL` (default `JSON` type). The API read it back as no contour, so nothing was visible, but `outline IS NULL` / `count(outline)` (the 14G.6 runbook counted contours that way) treated it as a contour. Fix: `JSON(none_as_null=True)` on `PhotoAnnotation.outline` — ORM behaviour only, no schema change, no migration. Regression `tests/test_stage14j_outline_null.py` (fails without the fix, also on SQLite). Contract §31 updated. **Production:** the code travels with the next backend deployment; rows cleared before it stay JSON `null` (harmless: reads as no contour); optional normalising `UPDATE` is in the contract and needs the owner's approval before it runs.
- **14J.3 — HTTP ownership guard (`tests/test_stage14j_http_guard.py`, 6 tests):** the photo operations of the running application (from OpenAPI) must equal an explicit list of 15 — a new photo route cannot appear without a probe; every photo route answers 401 without a token; every project-scoped route answers a foreign project exactly like a missing one (`PROJECT_NOT_FOUND`); a 29-row matrix for markers (foreign / other-project / pending / archived / cross-attachment / malformed / out-of-range / moved coordinate) and for INSPECTION / FINDING / WORK / lineage targets of another owner — fixed envelope, no storage key, sha256 or another owner's marker text; an existing foreign id answers byte-for-byte like an invented one (7 route pairs); counts belong to the project and owner only. **3 mutations** (marker not scoped to its attachment, archived photo accepts markers, counts not scoped to the project) each fail a test. No ownership defect found.
- **14J.4 — general gates.** Backend (SQLite) **4375 passed, 62 skipped** (opt-in PostgreSQL modules without `TEST_PG_URL`), 1 deselected (`test_stage14d2c_preflight`, sandbox runs as root, fails on the untouched tree too); with the PostgreSQL environment all opt-in modules pass. ### Stage 14F.4 — production deployment of 14F (2026-10-07, DEPLOYED `9ec1704` — A8 phone check PASS after an R2-key incident; **Stage 14F OWNER ACCEPTED 2026-10-07**)

**Result.** Migration `0034_finding_lineage` applied (`alembic current` = head), backend and frontend recreated, backup images rebuilt and a db-dump verified (A0–A6b executed per the runbook, each step approved). Rollback tags `:pre-14f4` exist. A7 (Telegram Menu Button cache-bust `?v=9ec1704`) is still open. A8 on the owner's phone: thumbnails and full photos show; photos can be added in the inspection header, on a checklist question and on a finding (the finding panel lists the lineage's photos); the object-wide photo count stays at the site photos (12) — **by design**, inspection evidence lives only in the inspection (14F.2 `site_only`; room totals unchanged).

**Incident after A5 (not caused by the release code).** Right after the backend was recreated, uploads failed (`MediaStorageMisconfigured`, R2 `AccessDenied` 403 on PUT) and, once uploads worked again, **no thumbnail or photo loaded on any device** (phone, phone through a Dutch VPN, a PC in Prague), while the same signed URL answered 200 from the VM. Diagnosis (read-only checks only): bucket / DB / objects intact (21 READY assets, 2 FAILED from the failed uploads); the API returned well-formed `https` signed URLs; the browser's request was byte-identical in the query; header bisect, protocol, colo (WAW / AMS / PRG vs FRA), WARP, VPN, Wi-Fi vs mobile all excluded; `curl` from a non-server address returned 403 and from the VM 200 → R2 was applying a **client-IP restriction** to the key that signs the URLs. The key in `.env.production` (`MEDIA_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` `ab8171…048b`) was IP-restricted to the server (`158.101.165.162/32`) — the only token with an IP filter was `plan-estimate-backup-media-read-prod` (the backup token; it also showed Object Read & Write, the docs call it read-only); this was inferred from the token list, not matched by token id. How the app came to use that key is not established. A presigned URL is signed with the token's credentials and **inherits its IP filter**, so every client except the server was refused.
**Fix (owner, production):** a new dedicated app token (Object Read & Write, only `plan-estimate-media-prod`, **no IP filter**) → both `MEDIA_S3_*` lines in `.env.production` replaced → `up -d --no-deps backend`. Verified: key id changed, `list` / `put` / `delete` OK from the server, a fresh signed URL returns 200 from a non-server address (`curl` on the owner's PC), the phone shows all thumbnails and uploads work. No code change.
**Lessons (written into the 14F.4 runbook, section 6):** (1) the app's R2 token must have **no IP filter**; backup tokens may keep one; (2) Cloudflare **Roll keeps the Access Key ID and changes only the secret**; (3) after any change of `MEDIA_S3_*`, check a signed URL from an address that is **not** the server (a `curl` from a PC) — a check from the VM alone cannot see this class of fault; (4) a diagnostic per layer (storage → URL → client) found it without touching data.
**Backup chain after the incident (owner, production, approved step by step).** `BACKUP_UPLOAD_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` in `upload.env` was also `ab8171…048b`, i.e. the Roll done during the incident had changed the secret of the backup token and the stored secret was stale. The valid secret (the one that passed `list/put/delete` before the key swap) was recovered from the `.env.production.bak2-*` copy and written into `upload.env` (copy of the old file kept, mode 0600, nothing printed); the backup token again lists the bucket (`list ok`). Full run: `db-dump` `run_id=20261007T203639Z-bfab5242 ready_count=26` (72 382-byte encrypted dump) → `upload complete … published objects=78 ready_assets=26` (78 = 26 × 3 derivatives) → `verify ok … mode=full size_checked=78 sha_checked=78` (all `exit 0`). 14F is therefore also covered by a fresh, verified backup.
**Closing steps (owner, production, 2026-10-07).** The backup token was set to Object Read only (IP filter kept): a check with the stored secret reads the bucket (`ok 3`) and is refused on write (`AccessDenied`). A7 done: `getChatMenuButton` returns `https://plan-estimate.pl/?v=9ec1704`. The only key ids in the VM's secret files are the app's (`97bfe5…6dab`, `.env.production`) and the backup's (`ab8171…048b`, `upload.env`); the copies with old secrets (`.env.production.bak-*`, `.bak2-*`, `upload.env.bak-*`) were `shred`-ed. **Still open (owner):** delete the unused old app token `plan-estimate-media-prod-app` in Cloudflare (the dev token `plan-estimate-photos-dev` stays); decide about `.env.production.pre-r2-20260928T174331Z` on the VM (a pre-R2 copy of the environment file, not part of this incident).

Runbook: `docs/STAGE_14F4_PRODUCTION_RUNBOOK_RU.md` (Russian; every production step needs the owner's explicit approval; the owner runs the commands and pastes the output). Order: A0 read-only state → A1 deploy-file diff (expected empty: compose / Caddy / Dockerfiles / requirements unchanged since the last backend deployment `4d4707a`; only 9 application files and migration `0034`) → A2 pre-deploy backup (recommended, existing images, head `0033`) → A3 `git pull --ff-only` → A4 `config --quiet` + build backend / frontend, rollback tags `:pre-14f4` → M0 head of the NEW image → **gate M (migration assessment: one column + index, one transaction, millisecond locks on a small table, reversible; rolling back the backend image without `alembic downgrade 0033` is unsafe for completing inspections because the old code cannot fill the NOT NULL column)** → A5 `up -d --no-deps backend` → A6 frontend → A6b rebuild backup images + `BACKUP_TOOL_COMMIT` → A7 Menu Button cache-bust → A8 phone check.

### Stage 14F.1 — durable finding lineage (2026-10-07, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY — not committed / deployed; backend with a migration)

Plan: `docs/STAGE_14F_FINDING_EVIDENCE_PLAN_RU.md`. First sub-stage of Stage 14F (design owner-approved: D14-26 / OD-5 / OD-11, `docs/STAGE_14_PHOTO_FIXATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §6.3 / §15.5). Extends accepted Stage 6 data in an isolated way: Stage 6 / 7 / 11 behaviour is unchanged.

- **Added:** migration `0034_finding_lineage` (reversible): `inspection_findings.lineage_id` UUID — add NULLable → deterministic backfill (one new UUID per `(inspection_id, question_id, finding_key)` group, shared by every row of the group, a NULL `question_id` counts as a value) → NOT NULL → index `ix_inspection_findings_lineage_id`. No finding UUID, flag, timestamp or other table is touched. `InspectionFinding.lineage_id` (model, default `uuid4` so existing direct constructions keep working), `InspectionFindingRead.lineage_id` (API), TS type `InspectionFinding.lineage_id`.
- **Changed:** `InspectionService._reconcile_findings`: a finding created after its source was resolved and confirmed again is still a NEW row (new UUID — Stage 7 / 11 signatures hash finding UUIDs and must not re-match dismissed recommendations) but takes the lineage of the most recent row of the same `(inspection_id, question_id, finding_key)` (resolved or not); a brand-new source gets a new lineage; confirmed active findings keep id and lineage as before.
- **Tests:** `test_stage14f1_finding_lineage.py` 12 (migration chain / single head, model, backfill grouping incl. NULL question, other question / inspection / key separate, nothing else touched, NOT NULL + index, up / down / up, no other table changes, rendered PostgreSQL DDL; API exposes lineage; resolve → re-confirm = new row, same lineage; unevenness kept; new inspection = new lineages; repeated cycles; the newest row decides). Mutations (no reuse, no per-inspection filter, group key without question / without inspection, no NOT NULL, no index, schema without the field, newest-wins) each fail a test. Backend full suite: 4088 passed, 54 skipped, 1 failed — `test_stage14d2c_preflight::test_workspace_preflight_passes_with_private_mounts_and_valid_passfile`, which fails identically on the untouched tree (sandbox environment, not related). `test_stage14c2_attachment_schema` head assertion updated to 0034. Frontend 79 files / 1769 tests, `tsc`, `vite build` PASS (two fixtures got the new field).
- **Found while testing:** the first backfill version read ids as plain strings on SQLite; the result columns are now typed `Uuid`, which is also the safe form on PostgreSQL.
- **Production:** a migration — deploy per `docs/PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK_RU.md` (inspect the migration, build backend, owner approves the migration assessment, recreate backend; the entrypoint applies `alembic upgrade head`); the backup images must be rebuilt after the migration (the backup tool enforces `alembic_version == head of its own image`). Nothing is deployed yet.

Instruction and phone check: `docs/STAGE_14E10_IN_APP_CAMERA_RU.md`. Frontend only; no backend, database or migration change. Owner decisions: build it (14E.9 result), series mode yes.

- **Added:** `utils/inAppCamera.ts` (support check = secure context + getUserMedia + ImageCapture, so iOS keeps the native `capture` input; rear-camera preview 1920×1440; still at the camera's largest size from `getPhotoCapabilities`, one retry with host defaults; torch; failure classes), `components/CameraCapture.tsx` (full-screen viewfinder in a portal above the photo viewer: series up to 10 shots with counter and last-shot thumbnail, "Gotowe (N)", torch, discard question when closing with shots, release / restart on `visibilitychange` and on a host-ended track, BackButton through the photo back registry, in-screen fallback to the phone's own picker with the reason), `photos.camera.*` strings (PL / RU), test fixtures (`cameraFixtures.ts`).

The canvas still path of the spike is not used (14 s, no EXIF).
- **Tests:** frontend 79 files / 1740 tests, `tsc`, `vite build` PASS (new: `inAppCamera` 25, `CameraCapture` 23, `PhotoPicker` 6 more); mutations (no explicit still size, wrong source, no visibility handling) each fail tests; one surviving mutation (the shutter guard at 10) is a second line behind the disabled button. Real Chromium with a fake camera inside the real app (wall card → viewfinder → 3 shots → "Gotowe" → 3 uploads queued and sent) at 320 / 390 / 412 px, PL / RU, light / dark: preview 1920×1440, no overflow, no control below 44 px, no console errors.
- **Owner check (2026-10-07, committed `26c0b07`, deployed):** all steps PASS **except step 3**: the still is square (3472×3472, not 4:3) and there is no pinch zoom ("фото квадратное, без возможности увеличить пальцами — это бы пригодилось"). So the explicit maximum size did not fix the crop. 14E.10 is NOT accepted yet; a diagnostics iteration follows (below), then the fix (full 4:3 still; zoom).
- **Follow-up diagnostics (in the 14E.9 screen, frontend only):** button "Test rozmiarów zdjęć i zoomu" — prints `getPhotoCapabilities`, a size ladder of `takePhoto` requests (default, 4624×3472 … 1920×1440), a zoom probe (separate stream with `zoom: true`, `applyConstraints` ×2) and an exact-4624×3472 stream with a default still. Tests: `cameraProbe` 19 (5 new), `CameraSpike` 13 (1 new); full frontend 79 files / 1746 tests, `tsc`, `vite build` PASS. Reading guide: `docs/STAGE_14E9_CAMERA_SPIKE_RU.md`, last section.
- **Diagnostics result (owner's phone, `353bf86` deployed, image `4e37ff528525`, rollback `:pre-a6u`):** `takePhoto` answers with the nearest size the host lists and there is no large 4:3 in the list: default / 4624×3472 / 4000×3000 → 3472×3472 square; 3264×2448 → 2160×3840 and 2560×1920 → 1296×2304 (16:9); only 1920×1440 → a true 4:3. No `capabilities.zoom` even with `zoom: true` (no hardware zoom); an exact 4624×3472 stream is `OverconstrainedError`. Details in `docs/STAGE_14E9_CAMERA_SPIKE_RU.md`.
- **Fix (14E.10 second iteration, implemented locally, not committed / deployed):** (1) `takeStill` searches the largest still size that really returns 4:3 (camera maximum → 4000×3000 → 3264×2448 → 2592×1944 → 2048×1536 → 1920×1440 → 1280×960), checking each answer's size from the JPEG header (`utils/jpegMeta.ts`), drops non-4:3 answers, remembers the working size in `localStorage` (re-searches if it stops working; keeps the largest answer and stops searching when the camera has no 4:3 at all); the first shot may take a few seconds, with a hint after ~2 s. (2) Digital zoom 1×–3× in the viewfinder: two-finger pinch or a 44 px pill (1× → 2× → 3×); the preview is scaled around its centre and the shot is the centre crop of the 4:3 still (re-encoded via canvas, EXIF block with the capture time copied back, orientation reset to 1; a crop failure is a failed shot, never a silent unzoomed photo). Resolution drops with zoom (from 1920×1440: 2× → 960×720). Strings `photos.camera.zoom` / `sizing` (PL / RU).
- **Tests (second iteration):** frontend 80 files / 1774 tests, `tsc`, `vite build` PASS (new: `jpegMeta` 7, `inAppCamera` 13 more, `CameraCapture` 8 more); mutations (tolerance, remembering, no-4:3 flag, forgetting stale size, crop offset, crop threshold, orientation reset, bitmap release, zoom clamp, zoom not passed to the shot, hint timer cleanup) each fail a test. Real Chromium with a fake camera at 390 px: preview scale 1 → 2 → 3 (pill and synthetic pinch), cropped JPEGs come out at 1/2 and 1/3 of the source size (1920×1080 and 1280×720 from 3840×2160), no console errors, video clipped inside the viewfinder, controls ≥ 44 px.
- **Owner check of the second iteration (2026-10-07, `df88e18` deployed, image `9a8e4ed94de9`, rollback `:pre-a6v`):** full 4:3 frame OK; the first shot takes longer and shows the "dobieram format 4:3…" hint as designed; zoom while shooting works well ("зум при съёмке работает хорошо"). **The owner accepted 14E.10 ("закрываем 14E.10").** The owner's further request (zoom while viewing a photo, full screen) is Stage 14E.11 above.

### Stage 14E.9 — in-app camera spike (2026-10-07, COMPLETE — result recorded; the diagnostics screen was removed after 14E.10 was accepted)

Instruction and decision table: `docs/STAGE_14E9_CAMERA_SPIKE_RU.md`. A sub-stage of Stage 14 (no change to the canonical roadmap); nothing is built beyond a diagnostic screen until the owner has seen its report.

- **Why:** Telegram on the owner's Android ignores `capture` and opens its gallery picker, so "Zrób zdjęcie" cannot take a photo. Question: can a page get the camera by itself (`getUserMedia`), and at what quality?
- **Added (frontend only):** `CameraSpike` screen (opened from the account window → "Diagnostyka kamery" / "Диагностика камеры"): starts the rear camera with three presets (max 4096×3072, 1920×1080, 1280×720), shows the preview, takes a still two ways (`ImageCapture.takePhoto` and a canvas frame), and prints a text report (environment, Telegram platform / version, permission state, granted size and frame rate, capability ranges, device list, size / type / EXIF of each still, track-ended events); the camera is released on stop, close and unmount. `utils/cameraProbe.ts` holds the helpers. PL / RU strings in the `cameraSpike` namespace. Nothing is uploaded or stored; no backend, database or migration change.
- **Tests:** frontend 77 files / 1686 tests, `tsc`, `vite build` PASS (new: `cameraProbe` 14, `CameraSpike` 12, `AccountModal` 5); a unit test found that `DOMException` is not always an `Error`, so `describeError` reads `name` / `message` by shape. Real Chromium with a fake camera (`--use-fake-device-for-media-stream`) at 320 / 390 px, PL / RU: stream granted, both stills taken, report complete, no overflow, no target below 44 px, no console errors.
- **Owner check (2026-10-07, Xiaomi 23122PCD1G, Android 16, Telegram-Android 12.10.6, Mini App API 9.6, WebView Chrome 153):** **the camera works inside the Mini App.** `permission camera=prompt` → the owner allowed it → `getUserMedia ok` (5.0 s including the permission tap), rear camera (`facing=environment`), 2 video inputs, torch available, zoom not. The max preset gave `settings: 3072x3472`, capabilities up to 4624×3472 (16 MP, 4:3). `ImageCapture.takePhoto` ok in 1.2 s: **JPEG 4.92 MB, 3472×3472 (square, 12 MP), with EXIF DateTimeOriginal** — the EXIF-based capture-source rule and `captured_at` would work. The canvas path took **14 s**, 2.04 MB, 3072×3472, **no EXIF** → unusable as the main path. The square size comes from asking 4096×3072 (the host picked a 1:1 mode): the real feature must read the capabilities / photo capabilities and ask for the sensor maximum (4624×3472) explicitly. Decision pending: build the real in-app camera (proposed as 14E.10) with `takePhoto`, torch toggle, burst mode and a fallback to the native file input.
- **Removed (after 14E.10 / 14E.11 acceptance):** `CameraSpike`, `utils/cameraProbe` (with the size-ladder / zoom / exact-stream probes), their tests, the account-window button "Diagnostyka kamery" and the `cameraSpike` / `auth.camera_diagnostics` strings; `AccountModal` is back to its pre-spike form. Frontend 79 files / 1768 tests, `tsc`, `vite build` PASS. The findings stay in `docs/STAGE_14E9_CAMERA_SPIKE_RU.md`.

  (icon buttons ≥ 44 × 44), the viewer exactly covers the screen, no console errors, no unstubbed API calls; screenshots were inspected. The harness was validated with a **negative control** (deliberately broken styles were detected; the first version

When the server is unreachable the browser's `fetch` rejects with a plain `TypeError`; the GET-first check of the queue then reported "unexpected error" instead of "no connection" → it now keeps the transport failure (network, retryable); a real HTTP error answer of the check (e.g. 401) is reported as such.     `reconcile()` that ends an item whose asset already exists and never starts a second concurrent POST.

    session, per-project view, `visibilitychange` / `online` reconcile, done / refetch subscriptions, storage refresh when the server stops the queue).
  - Locale namespace `photos` (section, picker, queue, viewer, category, caption, errors, storage) in `pl.json` and `ru.json`.

### Stage 14D.3 — Oracle Object Storage / IAM provisioning design (2026-10-04, DESIGN APPROVED — PROVISIONING NOT YET EXECUTED)

Design and owner Console runbook: `docs/STAGE_14D3_ORACLE_BACKUP_PROVISIONING.md`; summary in
`docs/STAGE_14D_BACKUP_RESTORE_PLAN.md` §16.8. Documentation only; **no OCI action, no code / Compose / Dockerfile
change, nothing provisioned.** Based on official Oracle documentation read 2026-10-03 (IAM Object Storage permission
reference, common policies, retention rules, versioning, instance principals, dynamic-group matching rules, S3
Compatibility API, Always Free resources, Object Storage overview).

- **Key facts:** create-only is IAM-enforceable (`OBJECT_CREATE` without `OBJECT_OVERWRITE` / `OBJECT_DELETE`);
  multipart needs `OBJECT_OVERWRITE` (single PutObject ≤ 50 GiB); retention rules and versioning are mutually
  exclusive; instance-principal rights are inherited by anyone on the instance.
- **Owner decisions (2026-10-04):** O1 Instance Principal for the uploader (API-key fallback only if impractical /
  not isolatable) — APPROVED; O2 local-only `backup` + separate future `backup-upload` — APPROVED; O3 native OCI SDK, not
  the S3 adapter — APPROVED; O4 — APPROVED WITH MANDATORY GATE (14D.4 must prove IMDS isolation on the production
  Docker host before any production-bucket uploader authority; uploader policy phased: drill only now, production after
  14D.4 PASS + owner approval); O5 create-only IAM + versioning, no retention rule / lifecycle deletion — APPROVED; O6
  restore authority off the VM — APPROVED; O7 compartment `plan-estimate-backup` — APPROVED; O8 provider-independent DB
  copy — **DEFERRED HARDENING** (not a 14D gate). Buckets renamed to `plan-estimate-backup-prod` /
  `plan-estimate-backup-drill`.
- **IAM statements remain PROPOSED** until Console validation and the 14D.4 empirical proof (create allowed; HEAD /
  GET / list as designed; overwrite, delete, version delete, bucket mutation denied; native `if-none-match: *`; restore
  principal read-only; IMDS isolation).
- **Not done:** any provisioning (owner, manual), env files, uploader tooling, 14D.4, the ARM64 gate.
- **Status**: **DESIGN APPROVED — PROVISIONING NOT YET EXECUTED.** 14D.4 not started. Production unchanged; uploads OFF.
