### Archive cleanup AC-1 — the trash for archived photos (2026-10-16, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY on branch `backlog-archive-cleanup` — not a roadmap stage; needs migration `0056`; not deployed)
Plan: `docs/ARCHIVE_CLEANUP_PLAN_RU.md` §4, §10; checks: `docs/ARCHIVE_CLEANUP_AC0_RU.md`. **Nothing is deleted in AC-1**: the trash is a state of the archive (files in R2 and in the backups are untouched; the final deletion is AC-2).
- **Database:** migration `0056_photo_trash` (revision id 16 chars, reversible, lossless): `photo_attachments.trashed_at timestamptz NULL`, `CHECK (trashed_at IS NULL OR archived_at IS NOT NULL)` (the trash is a state of the archive), index `(project_id, trashed_at)`. The downgrade drops the column; the attachments stay archived. Verified on a real PostgreSQL 16 scratch cluster (loopback, `pe_scratch_test_ac1`, removed afterwards): `alembic upgrade head` → `0056_photo_trash`, downgrade to `0055`, upgrade again, the CHECK refuses a trashed-but-not-archived row.
- **Backend:** `PhotoAttachmentService.trash_attachment` (only an ARCHIVED attachment; idempotent; else 409 `PHOTO_ATTACHMENT_NOT_ARCHIVED`) and `untrash_attachment` (back to the archive; idempotent); `restore_attachment` from the trash goes straight to the active photos; routes `POST /projects/{id}/photo-attachments/{id}/trash` and `/untrash`; the list has `trashed=true` (exclusive with `archived`, 422 otherwise) and the archive view no longer shows what is in the trash; `trashed_at` in `PhotoAttachmentRead`. The storage port is untouched (`MediaStorage` still has no delete; AC-2 adds a separate `MediaPurger`, see AC-0 F3).
- **Frontend:** in the photo section the archive has two views, "Archiwum | Kosz" (RU "Архив | Корзина") with a hint that nothing in the trash is deleted; the viewer of an archived photo offers "Do kosza" (with a note), the viewer in the trash offers "Wyjmij z kosza" and "Przywróć"; moving between the archive and the trash changes no badge count; PL / RU texts. A real Chromium check found and fixed one defect (after "Do kosza" the viewer index stayed and the viewer reopened by itself in the trash view) — regression test added.
- **Tests:** backend `test_ac1_photo_trash.py` (8: an active photo cannot be trashed; views archive / trash / active; nothing deleted — the storage keys are the same; untrash idempotent; restore from the trash; archive of a trashed photo keeps it trashed; exclusive views 422; other attachments of the same asset untouched; foreign / unknown ids 404) and `test_ac1_photo_trash_migration.py` (4); the seven "single head" assertions and `test_stage14c2_attachment_schema` now know `0056`. Frontend: 6 new tests in `PhotoSection.test.tsx` (two views and their server parameters, "Do kosza", "Wyjmij z kosza", restore from the trash +1, no trash button on an active photo, the viewer-reopen regression), mutation-checked (the request parameter and the viewer fix).
- **Mobile (real Chromium, PL / RU × 320 / 390 / 412 px, 24 checks):** archive view with the two views, viewer of an archived photo, trash view, viewer of a trashed photo — no horizontal scroll, buttons ≥ 43 px, long RU texts wrap.
- **Deferred inside the plan:** a trash tab on the "Archiwum" screen that gathers the trashed photos of all objects (AC-1 puts the trash where the photo was taken — the per-section archive); the final deletion (AC-2).


### Archive cleanup AC-2 — deleting a photo from the trash for good (2026-10-16, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY on branch `backlog-archive-cleanup` — not a roadmap stage; needs migration `0057`; not deployed)
Plan: `docs/ARCHIVE_CLEANUP_PLAN_RU.md` §7.1, §9; findings it follows: `docs/ARCHIVE_CLEANUP_AC0_RU.md` (F1 the three places that point to photos, F3 a separate purge port). **This is the first step that deletes data**: only from the trash, after a preview, with a confirmation; nothing is run against production by the code — the owner decides when it is deployed and what is deleted.
- **Port:** `MediaPurger` (`delete_objects(keys)`, an already-missing key is a success) is a **separate port** from `MediaStorage`, which still has no delete (guarded by the old test, now with an extra assertion that the storage objects have no `delete_objects` either); adapters `S3MediaPurger` (R2, over the storage's lazy client, provider errors mapped to `MediaStorage*`), `DisabledMediaPurger`, `InMemoryMediaPurger` (tests); dependency `get_media_purger` (overridden in tests).
- **Database:** migration `0057_purge_ledger` (id 17 chars, reversible but the **downgrade refuses while the ledger has rows**): table `purge_ledger` — one row per deleted file set (the three storage keys, the original's SHA-256, sizes, time, `storage_state` and `backup_state` PENDING / DONE with CHECKs, unique per asset), **no foreign keys and no content or names** (the duty to clean the backups outlives every other row). Verified on a real PostgreSQL 16 scratch cluster (loopback, removed afterwards): `alembic upgrade head` → `0057`, downgrade / upgrade, then a real purge through the service with the real foreign keys (asset, attachment and markers gone, ledger `DONE` / `PENDING`), and the downgrade refusing with a ledger row.
- **Rules (`domain/rules/purge_rules.py`, pure):** a photo that a protocol of the object still points to is not deleted — concealed works (`photo_ids`), downtime (`photo_ids`), acceptance (the remarks of `surfaces`, read in the stored dict shape and also as a list) — in every status except `ARCHIVED` (a DRAFT blocks too: the owner removes the photo from the draft first).
- **Service (`PhotoPurgeService`):** `preview` (no side effects: markers, other uses of the file, files 0 / 3, bytes, blockers, can_purge); `purge`: only an attachment in the trash, not blocked; **one transaction** deletes the markers and the attachment and, when it was the **last use of the file**, the file's row and writes the ledger row; **only then** the three objects are removed and the ledger row marked `DONE`. A failure of the storage after the commit loses nothing: the ledger row stays `PENDING`, the answer says `storage_pending`, and a retry (`POST /photo-purge/retry`, and automatically before every purge) finishes it. A file with another use stays until its last use is deleted.
- **API:** `GET /projects/{id}/photo-attachments/{id}/purge-preview`, `POST .../purge` (409 `PHOTO_PURGE_NOT_TRASHED` / `PHOTO_PURGE_BLOCKED` with the blockers / `PHOTO_PURGE_CONFLICT`), `GET /photo-purge/status`, `POST /photo-purge/retry` (all per owner; a foreign project or photo is a 404 like a missing one; the HTTP guard test knows the four routes).
- **Frontend:** in the trash view the viewer offers "Usuń na zawsze…" (RU "Удалить навсегда…"); it opens a panel **"Co zostanie usunięte"** with the numbers the server computed (files and size, markers, the backups note, the Telegram note, "this cannot be undone"), the protocols that block it (the button is off), "Anuluj" as the main button and a red "Usuń na zawsze"; after the deletion the photo leaves the list and no badge count changes; when the storage did not answer the section says the files follow later. PL / RU texts.
- **Tests:** backend 33 new (`test_ac2_purge_rules` 5, `test_ac2_photo_purge` 19 incl. 9 protocol-protection cases, `test_ac2_purge_ledger_migration` 4, `test_ac2_s3_purger` 5) — mutation-checked (the trash check, the "last use" rule); frontend 8 new in `PhotoSection.test.tsx` (the panel numbers, cancel deletes nothing, confirm, blockers, kept file, pending note, server refusal, no button outside the trash) — mutation-checked (the confirm button's off state).
- **Mobile (real Chromium, PL / RU × 320 / 390 / 412 px, 24 checks):** the trash viewer with the new button, the panel for a deletable and for a blocked photo, the confirmation call — no horizontal scroll, buttons ≥ 43 px, long RU texts wrap.
- **Not in AC-2 (by the plan):** removing the copies from the Oracle backups and teaching the backup check / restore about the ledger (AC-3: the owner-run script, the restore replay, a new backup run after the cleaning); the trash and deletion of rooms, surfaces, openings, inspections (AC-4), of objects and clients (AC-5).


### Archive cleanup AC-3 — removing the backup copies of deleted photos; the backup tooling learns the ledger (2026-10-16, IMPLEMENTED LOCALLY on branch `backlog-archive-cleanup` — not a roadmap stage; no migration; nothing run against Oracle or production)
Plan: `docs/ARCHIVE_CLEANUP_PLAN_RU.md` §7; runbook: **`docs/ARCHIVE_PURGE_RUNBOOK_RU.md`** (the order, the OCI access for the cleaning, the rehearsal, the restore after it). The backup **uploader and its rights are unchanged**: it still cannot delete; the owner's separate tool does, off the VM.
- **The ledger as a file (`app/backup/purge_ledger.py`):** canonical JSON lines (`plan-estimate/purge-ledger/v1`: header with count, one line per deleted file set — three keys, the original's SHA-256, sizes, time; no content, no owner, no project). The reader is **strict because a wrong line would delete the wrong object**: every key must be exactly one of the three keys of its asset under `photos/v1/<asset>/` (`original.<ext>` / `display.jpg` / `thumb.jpg`), canonical UUIDs, a valid SHA-256, positive sizes, no duplicate, the count must match (12 refusal cases tested, one found by a mutation: the original of another asset).
- **Server side (`python -m app.cli.purge_ledger`, inside the backend container):** `export [--pending-only] [--out]` writes the file from `purge_ledger`; `mark-done --report` marks `backup_state=DONE` only for the file sets the owner's tool found clean **in the production bucket** (a drill-bucket report marks nothing; idempotent; unknown ids ignored).
- **The owner's tool (`scripts/purge_backup_objects.py`, workstation, OCI SDK):** dry run by default (lists the versions that exist, deletes nothing); `--execute --report` asks for a typed phrase (**`УДАЛИТЬ ИЗ БЭКАПА ДА`** for production, `РЕПЕТИЦИЯ ДА` for the drill bucket — the drill phrase does not open production); accepts only `plan-estimate-backup-prod` / `plan-estimate-backup-drill`; deletes **every version and delete marker by its version id** of exactly the ledger's three keys (never a delete without a version id, which would only add a marker; a longer name sharing the prefix is ignored), lists again and fails if anything remains; one failed set does not stop the others; `runs/` and `db/` are never named. Report: `plan-estimate/purge-backup-report/v1`. `scripts/purge_rehearsal_ledger.py` builds the rehearsal ledger from complete file sets of the **drill bucket only** (read-only).
- **verify:** `verify_run_in_target(..., purged_keys=)` / `verify --purge-ledger FILE`: a manifest line of a purged key that is gone from the target is **expected** (`purged_absent`), one still there is checked as usual (`purged_present`); damage that the ledger does not list is still a problem. New counts in the report: `purged_absent`, `purged_present`.
- **restore:** `restore_media(..., purged_keys=)` never copies a purged object back, whether or not the backup still holds it (`purged_skipped`); `restore_run(..., purge_ledger=)` then **replays the ledger on the restored database** as a last step after the media step has succeeded (`app/backup/purge_replay.py`: one transaction removes the markers, the attachments and the file sets of exactly the ledger's assets, then records the ledger rows; idempotent; a failure changes nothing and is `REPLAY_FAILED`); `restore --purge-ledger FILE`. Without a ledger the chain is exactly what it was.
- **Tests:** 57 new in `tests/test_ac3_*.py` — the file (strictness, round trips, the report), verify (4), restore media (3), the replay (the statements, the single transaction, a failure keeps the database as it was), the whole chain (replay after media, never after a failed media step, `REPLAY_FAILED`), the server export / mark-done (prod / drill, idempotent, the command's refusals), the owner's tool (13: dry run, rehearsal deletes only the ledger objects, markers, prefix names, phrases, the two buckets, repeat is safe, a failed set, versions that do not go away, nothing secret printed) and the rehearsal ledger; **mutation-checked** (verify and restore ignoring the ledger, the replay skipped, a foreign key accepted, the name filter, the version id, the confirmation, any bucket).
- **Rehearsal in the Oracle drill bucket — PASS (2026-10-16, owner, from a throwaway `python:3.12` container on the workstation; no Docker on the production VM):** access created in the OCI console (user `plan-estimate-purge-operator`, group and policy `plan-estimate-backup-purge[-policy]` in the compartment `plan-estimate-backup`; the API key lives only on the owner's computer and is deleted after the work). Steps: the rehearsal ledger from the drill bucket (`file_sets=1`, **8** complete file sets in the bucket) → dry run (`bucket_kind=drill`, **3 versions found** — one per object —, `deleted=0`) → deletion after the typed phrase `РЕПЕТИЦИЯ ДА` (**3 versions deleted**, report written) → the same dry run again (**`versions found=0`, clean**) → the rehearsal ledger rebuilt from the bucket (`of 7 complete`): **exactly one file set was removed, the other seven stay**. Findings during the setup (all on the owner's side or in the instructions, not in the tools): the first refusals were `ServiceError` without a reason, so b47ad60 makes the tools print the HTTP status and the OCI error code (neither is secret); the cause was the missing policy / group membership (`404 BucketNotFound` is how OCI says "not authorised"). Not exercised live: `mark-done` with a rehearsal report (covered by the tests; it needs AC-3 deployed on the VM) — to be seen at the first real cleaning.
- **Owner steps that remain (not done by me):** create the OCI group / policy `plan-estimate-backup-purge` (runbook §2), run the rehearsal on the drill bucket (§3) and send the result; the first real cleaning only after AC-1 … AC-3 are deployed (migrations `0056`, `0057`, backup A9 first) and a photo was really deleted.


### Archive cleanup — the release package for AC-1 … AC-3 and 19H (2026-10-16, PREPARED — not deployed)
Files: `docs/ARCHIVE_CLEANUP_DEPLOY_RU.sh`, `docs/ARCHIVE_CLEANUP_RUNBOOK_RU.md` (order, estimate, rollback, the phone checklist). The script is the full one (G0 checks → G1 build with the tags `pre-ac` → **gate M "МИГРАЦИИ 0056 0057 ДА"** → G2 backend and migrations → G3 frontend → G4 Telegram menu button): it refuses without a backup younger than 72 h, a database exactly on `0055`, exactly the two new migrations, no change of the images / dependencies / compose / environment example, only whitelisted paths; G2 checks the schema (column, CHECK, index, table, an empty ledger), the Stage 19 schemas, the knowledge catalogue and calendar texts, the eight new routes, **the purger being the S3 one**, the calendar loop as it was (settings, bot token, no "not started" error — not the INFO log line, see the 19 deployment note), the S3 key / bucket, and that **no data row changed**; G3 checks the served bundle for the offline database, the sync screen, the calendar and the purge panel. **Dry run on stubs of `docker` / `curl` over a real git origin: 1 full pass + 12 refusals** (wrong gate answer, database not on 0055, build fails, wrong schema after the migration, the purger not S3, bundle without the purge panel, the migration not in the log, data changed, alembic not at 0057, API without the routes, loop on but no token, backend unhealthy) — each stops at the right step.
**Finding (checked on a real PostgreSQL 16 scratch cluster): the rollback by images alone does NOT work once migrations are applied** — the entrypoint runs `alembic upgrade head`, and an old image fails with "Can't locate revision" on a database at a newer revision. The Stage 18 runbook's statement "rolling the backend image back without the migration is safe" was wrong (never exercised). The release's rollback order is therefore: downgrade the migrations with the NEW image first (`run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint alembic backend downgrade 0055_project_notes`, lossless; the downgrade of `0057` refuses while the ledger has rows), then retag both images, then `up`. The window for the rollback closes at the first real deletion of a photo (the ledger gets a row): the real deletion is a separate step after the acceptance (runbook §5, item 8). The backup images must be rebuilt for the head `0057` by the next A9 (`BACKUP_BRANCH=backlog-archive-cleanup BACKUP_HEAD=0057_purge_ledger`).

### Archive cleanup AC-5b — deleting an archived object for good (2026-10-17, DONE locally, not deployed; goes out together with AC-4a / AC-5a as the release 3)
Owner's decision: C after A + B; no trash for the object (the archive is the reversible step). **Added (no migration):** `GET /api/projects/{id}/purge-preview` and `POST /api/projects/{id}/purge` (`ProjectPurgeService`, `purge_rules.object_blockers`, `schemas/project_purge.py`, `endpoints/project_purge.py`). Only an ARCHIVED object. **What holds an object** (it cannot be deleted, only archived): a contract ISSUED / SIGNED, a handover / concealed-works / decision / acceptance protocol ISSUED, a downtime notice NOTICED / CLOSED; drafts and archived documents do not hold and go with the object. **Order (the same as one photo, AC-2):** ONE transaction deletes the markers, attachments and file rows of every photo of the object (by the ids it read, so a photo added meanwhile is not silently dropped), writes one ledger row (`PENDING`) per file set and deletes the object -- the database removes everything below it by `ON DELETE CASCADE`; a photo that appeared meanwhile makes the foreign key `RESTRICT` refuse, the transaction rolls back and nothing is lost (409 `PROJECT_PURGE_CONFLICT`); then, outside the transaction, the files leave the storage and the ledger rows become `DONE`, a failure leaves them `PENDING` for the same retry (`/api/photo-purge/retry`, also run before every deletion). **Verified on a real PostgreSQL 16 scratch cluster (migrated to head): the foreign keys below an object are all `CASCADE` except `SET NULL` ones inside the same subtree and `RESTRICT` on the photo tables (which the service deletes first); no table keeps rows of the object without a foreign key (except the ledger, on purpose); a raw delete of an object with photos is refused (RESTRICT); the service deleted an object with 4 photos, a room, wall, door, a contract and a protocol (every table with `project_id` shows 0 rows of it) and left another object whole; 4 ledger rows, all storage `DONE`, backup `PENDING`, the deleted keys equal the ledger keys.** **Decisions I took (the owner may change them):** no tombstone of the documents journal (numbers are date-time based, never re-issued); restoring an OLD dump brings back the rows of a deleted object (its photos are removed again by the ledger replay, the object stays without photos) -- replaying object deletions on restore is deferred and written into the runbook; the confirmation is a tick "Rozumiem, że tej operacji nie można cofnąć" (a 44 px field) plus a red button, no typing of a name (mobile). **Frontend:** "Usuń na zawsze…" on every archived object (the Objects tab of the Archive): the panel with the counts the server made (only non-zero lines), the documents sent to the client (their copies in Telegram chats stay), the note about the backups, the reasons that hold an object (a list in the owner's words), the tick, "Anuluj" / "Usuń na zawsze"; after it the lists and the photo tab are read again; PL / RU texts.
Tests: backend `test_ac5b_project_purge.py` (27: archived only; the preview; the deletion of everything below and the files, the other object whole; no photos; a storage failure and the retry; a photo that appears meanwhile stops it all or nothing; 17 document cases; another owner / missing / no sign-in) and `test_ac5b_object_rules.py` (20); **four mutations** (no blockers, assets deleted by project instead of by the read ids, no archived check, no ledger) each made tests fail; full backend run (see the commit); frontend `ArchiveStructure.test.tsx` (+10: counts, the tick gate, the pending-files note, held object, cancel, not archived, a conflict, a document issued meanwhile, other failure, empty object, Russian); **two mutations** (the tick not required, the lists not read again) each made a test fail; frontend 3200 passed, `tsc`, `vite build`; real Chromium 320 / 390 / 412 PL and RU with a very long object name: 18 measurements, no overflow, controls >= 44 px.


### Archive cleanup AC-4b — deleting an archived room or surface for good (2026-10-17, DONE locally, not deployed; the release 4)
The owner's request after the release 3 (screenshots of the tabs "Pomieszczenia" / "Powierzchnie"): "add the deletion for a surface and a room". **Added (no migration):** `GET /api/projects/{id}/rooms/{room}/purge-preview` + `POST .../purge` and `GET/POST /api/projects/{id}/rooms/{room}/surfaces/{surface}/purge-preview|purge` (`StructurePurgeService`, `purge_rules.structure_blockers`, `schemas/structure_purge.py`, `endpoints/structure_purge.py`; `PhotoPurgeService.protocol_refs` made public). Only an ARCHIVED room / surface, no trash. **What holds it** (nothing is deleted until the owner archives the document first): any document that is NOT archived and points to it -- a concealed-works protocol (by its surface), an acceptance protocol (by room or surface), a downtime notice (by room), a work of an adjacent trade (by room) -- and a photo of it that such a protocol uses as evidence; an ARCHIVED document holds nothing (the rule of AC-2). The estimates are snapshots (their lines only lose the link to the surface): not a hold, told in the preview. **Order (the same as an object / a photo):** ONE transaction deletes the markers and attachments of every photo in the room / surface (its surfaces, openings, inspections and their findings too), the file rows that no OTHER photo still uses (a file used elsewhere stays), writes one ledger row (`PENDING`) per file set removed, cancels the waiting calendar reminders about it and deletes the room / surface -- the database removes everything below by `ON DELETE CASCADE`; a photo / use added meanwhile makes `RESTRICT` refuse and the transaction rolls back (409 `STRUCTURE_PURGE_CONFLICT`); then the files leave the storage and the ledger rows become `DONE` (a failure leaves them `PENDING` for the same retry). **Verified on a real PostgreSQL 16 scratch cluster (migrated to head):** a raw delete of a room with photos is refused (RESTRICT); a room with a surface, an opening, an inspection with a finding and photos in five contexts (room, surface, opening, inspection, finding) was deleted by the service -- the rows of the room, surface, opening, inspection and finding are all gone, 5 attachments and their markers removed, 4 file sets removed and ledgered (the 5th file is also used by an object-level attachment and STAYED, with that attachment), the deleted keys equal the ledger keys, and the other room with its own full set stayed whole; then an archived surface of the other room was deleted on its own, leaving its room and its room photo. **Frontend:** "Usuń na zawsze…" on every row of the two tabs: the panel with the server's counts (only non-zero lines: surfaces, openings, inspections, photos with files and size, markers), the estimate lines that stay, the backups note, the reasons that hold it, the tick and the red button; the lists, the numbers and the photo tab are read again afterwards; PL / RU texts.

The downgrade **refuses while any record exists** (the owner's money records are never dropped silently). **Domain:** `domain/rules/payment_totals.py` (pure: the summary -- invoiced, received, expenses, the unpaid rest of the invoices, left to receive, the cash result -- and the state of an invoice PAID / PARTIAL / OVERDUE / OPEN; archived records count for nothing, a payment settles only the invoice it is tied to, the due day itself is not late, every sum is `Decimal` with two places) and `domain/services/payment_service.py` (owner-scoped; create under an id chosen by the phone and safe to repeat (`find_repeat`, Stage 19C); the rules of a kind; update that never changes the kind; archive / restore, no erasing; the agreed amount and **the hint** = the total of the accepted estimate, else of the final one, never becoming the agreed amount by itself). **API** (`endpoints/payments.py`, schemas with money as a string with exactly two places): `GET /api/projects/{id}/payments?kind=&include_archived=` (items + summary + agreed amount), `POST`, `PATCH /{payment_id}`, `POST /{payment_id}/archive|restore`, `GET|PUT /api/projects/{id}/finance`. **AC-5b:** the preview of deleting an object counts the records (`payments`, archived included); they go with the object by the cascade (they do not hold it). ### "Faktury i zaliczki" IA-4 -- the settlements without a signal (2026-10-17, DONE locally, not deployed; branch `backlog-finance-encryption`)
Plan: `docs/INVOICES_ADVANCES_PLAN_RU.md` v2 (a backlog item, not a roadmap stage). **Frontend only: no migration, no backend change** (the create of a record has taken the id of the phone and been safe to repeat since IA-1). ### "Faktury i zaliczki" IA-5 -- the due day of an invoice is a reminder of the calendar (2026-10-17, DONE locally, not deployed; branch `backlog-finance-encryption`)
Plan: `docs/INVOICES_ADVANCES_PLAN_RU.md` v2 (a backlog item, not a roadmap stage). **No migration** (the kind of a reminder is a free string column). A new event kind `INVOICE_DUE` ("an invoice of the settlements of the object is due"), separate from `PAYMENT_TERM` (the advance of the contract, § 6, which stays off by default): the owner can switch the invoices off without touching the contract's terms. It is derived, like every other event, by a pure function from the facts (`invoice_events`): an invoice that is **not archived, has a due day and is not paid in full** (the same `invoice_standings` as the summary; a part payment does not close it). **By default it sends a message** (a decision of mine, switchable in the settings of the calendar like every kind): **3 days ahead and on the day itself**, in the morning digest, never in the quiet hours; the text names the invoice ("Termin zapłaty faktury: FV 7/2026" / "Срок оплаты фактуры: ..."; its number, else what it is for, cut to 60 characters; `{what}` is the only placeholder a text may carry and a name with braces in it is a value, never a template). The calendar shows the day whether or not the message is on; an overdue invoice is shown, and no late message is made for it (a rule of Stage 18C). **The reminders follow every change at once:** creating, changing (amount, due day) or archiving / restoring a record -- including a payment that pays the invoice in full or is taken back -- reconciles the object's reminders (the periodic pass of Stage 18D is the net under it, and a fault in the calendar is logged and never undoes the record). Moving the due day moves the reminders, clearing it or paying cancels them, restoring brings the same rows back; an archived object keeps none (Stage 18C); they go with the object when it is deleted (their foreign key cascades). The form of an invoice says that the due day becomes a reminder (PL / RU). Frontend: the title of an event carries `{what}`, the settings list the new kind.
Files: `domain/calendar/events.py` (`INVOICE_DUE`, `InvoiceDue`, `invoice_events`, lead days, default push), `domain/calendar/texts.json` and `messages.py` (the text with `{what}`), `domain/services/calendar_service.py` (`_invoice_events`), `domain/services/payment_service.py` (`_calendar_follows`), `utils/calendarFormat.ts`, `PaymentForm.tsx`, locales.
Tests: `test_ia5_invoice_due.py` (25: the pure event, three days ahead and the day, switching off, the message in both languages, a name with braces, the real routes -- a part and a full payment, archive and restore, a moved or cleared due day, a changed amount, the settings and the agenda, an archived object, a fault of the calendar, the periodic pass, another owner), `test_ac5b_project_purge.py` (+1: the reminders go with the object), the words test of Stage 18D (the new event and the one placeholder); frontend `calendarFormat.test.ts` (7), `CalendarScreen.test.tsx` (+2), `ProjectPayments.test.tsx` (+1). **11 mutations, all caught.**
Verification: full backend 5939 passed (the one known failure `test_stage14d2c_preflight`: the sandbox runs as root), full frontend 162 files / 3485 tests (the one older unhandled error of `ProjectDocuments` stays), `tsc` and `vite build` PASS, real Chromium at 320 / 390 / 412 px PL + RU: 54 + 18 layout checks of the screens with the new hint. Not deployed.
**Deployment:** IA-1 .. IA-5 are ONE release with two migrations (0058, 0059); IA-5 adds backend code and no schema. After it the first reconciliation (the next periodic pass, or the first change of a record) queues the reminders of the invoices that already exist.

The summary now carries `expenses_by_category`: the parts of `expenses`, **made on the server** by `payment_totals.summarize` (only the categories that have a live expense, in the fixed order of `CATEGORIES`, the expenses without a category last as `null`; archived records and other kinds are in no part; the parts always add up to `expenses`). A category can be set, changed and cleared (`null`) on an expense and is refused (`PAYMENT_INVALID`) on any other kind; a word that is not a category is a 422; sending the same expense again is safe and with another category it is the usual id conflict. Offline: a waiting expense carries its category, an invoice made offline has none, a change of the category lies over the record. **The statement "Rozliczenie" (IA-6a) still never prints expenses**, categories included.

### "Faktury i zaliczki" IA-7 -- the settlements in the archive: restore and delete for good; the dark-theme canvas (2026-10-18, DONE locally, not deployed; branch `backlog-finance-encryption`)
Plan: `docs/INVOICES_ADVANCES_PLAN_RU.md` v2 (a backlog item, not a roadmap stage). **Born of the owner's phone check of the IA-1..IA-6 release (2026-10-17/18):** (1) the archive page has no place for archived invoices, advances and expenses, and they could not be deleted; (2) in the dark theme the page below a short screen was white. **No migration** (the database already has `ON DELETE SET NULL` for the link of a payment to an invoice and `RESTRICT` for the photos of a record).
**The archive tab "Faktury i zaliczki" (PL) / "Счета и авансы" (RU):** lists the archived records of all objects in work (the object named, the kind, the sum, the day, the number, the shop, the category, the number of receipt photos; the first 200, the total whole; nothing of an archived object, nothing of another owner), with "Przywróć" (the route of the record) and "Usuń na zawsze…". **Deleting for good** follows the room (AC-4b) and the photo (AC-2): only an ARCHIVED record; the server first counts what goes (receipt / invoice photos with their files and markers, and -- for an invoice -- the payments that settled it: **they stay with their money and lose only the link**) and the owner reads it, ticks "I understand" and confirms. One transaction deletes the markers, the attachments, the file rows no other photo still uses (one ledger row `PENDING` each), unlinks the payments and deletes the record; a photo added meanwhile makes the `RESTRICT` refuse and nothing is lost (409 `PAYMENT_PURGE_CONFLICT`); then the objects leave the storage and the ledger rows become `DONE` (a storage fault leaves them `PENDING`, the retry of Stage AC-2 finishes them). A record in work is refused (409 `PAYMENT_NOT_ARCHIVED`). The sums of the object follow by themselves (they are made from the records that remain). This is a deliberate step away from "a record is never erased": the owner asked for it, and only from the archive after the preview.
**The dark theme:** the body carried `bg-gray-50` (a Tailwind class that outranked the theme colour), so the canvas below the app's own block was light grey; the class is gone and `html` takes `--tg-theme-bg-color` too. (The white CARDS on the dark background are the design of the whole app and are not changed here.)
Files: `domain/services/payment_purge_service.py`, `api/v1/endpoints/payment_purge.py` (`GET /api/archive/payments`, `GET .../payments/{id}/purge-preview`, `POST .../payments/{id}/purge`), `schemas/payment_purge.py`, `domain/exceptions.py`, `main.py`; frontend `components/ArchiveScreen.tsx` (the tab), `components/ArchivePaymentDelete.tsx`, `api/payments.ts`, `types/payment.ts`, locales PL / RU, `index.html`, `index.css`.

It removes **only the line of the journal**: the document it recorded (an estimate, a contract, a protocol ...) and the PDF in the chat stay (no file is kept, and nothing else reads a row after its attempt has ended -- checked in the issuer). A row whose attempt is still running is refused (409 `DOCUMENT_IN_PROGRESS`, the background render writes its result into it); an attempt left pending past the time limit has ended (`get` ends it first) and can go. Other owner / other object / unknown -> 404. The button "Usuń z dziennika…" is on every sent / failed row of the journal of all objects (the screen of the owner's screenshot) and of the journal of one object, with a question that says what goes and what stays and a tick. The running number of the objects' documents (`project_seq`) is not renumbered: deleting the newest row of an object lets the next document take its number; the time number (`KOSZ/2026/10/18/1000`) is given by the time. `test_dj1_journal_delete.py` (10), frontend `SentDocuments.test.tsx` (+6), `ProjectDocuments.test.tsx` (+1); the error-code scan of Stage 15F.3 caught a code without sentences once (the exception is named `DocumentInProgressError` now, the PL / RU sentence is there).

### Client data encryption, EN-1: the spike page "Test zabezpieczeń" (2026-10-18, DONE locally, not deployed; branch `backlog-client-encryption`; not a roadmap stage)
**Merge:** on the owner's "слияние, пуш" `backlog-finance-encryption` was fast-forward merged into `main` (`3cecb69`) and both were pushed; the switch of the VM to `main` is still the owner's separate decision. The new branch `backlog-client-encryption` starts from `main`.
**Decisions of the owner (2026-10-18):** start with EN-1; **the object name is encrypted**; **AAD = "table.column"** (variant (a)). Recorded with the findings of the inventory in the plan (`docs/CLIENT_DATA_ENCRYPTION_PLAN_RU.md`, section 0): `cryptography` is not in `requirements.txt` of the web image (a dependency change needs its own deployment script); the client search (`ilike` over four fields) moves to Python after decryption; two indexes lose their meaning; two `order_by(Project.name)` move to Python; a `TypeDecorator` cannot know the row id, hence AAD = column only (the limit is written down: a ciphertext can be moved between rows of the same column and owner; it matters for a writer of the database, not for a leak of a dump).
**EN-1 built:** `security/probe.ts` -- nine checks of THIS phone (the environment and the Bot API version; WebCrypto AES-256-GCM with the refusal of a damaged ciphertext; PBKDF2 at 100k / 300k / 600k rounds; Argon2id at 19 MiB t2 and 64 MiB t3 through `hash-wasm` 4.12.0, a chunk of its own loaded only on the page; CloudStorage write / read / list / remove; the size wall of a CloudStorage value at 1024 / 4096 / 4097; SecureStorage; DeviceStorage; BiometricManager), the two taps (the access to biometrics, the finger), the marker per storage (what survives a reinstall or a new phone), and the report to copy. The page is the last item of the main menu ("Test zabezpieczeń" / "Тест защиты"), **touches no client data and sends nothing to the server**; the probes write and remove `en1_*` values, the marker stays only on the owner's tap. Every call that answers through a callback has an 8-second timeout (an unknown API in an old client is a result, not a hang).
Files: `frontend/src/security/probe.ts`, `components/SecurityProbe.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `types/telegram.ts`, locales PL / RU, `package.json` + `package-lock.json` (one dependency). Tests: `probe.test.ts` (38), `SecurityProbe.test.tsx` (12), `App.security.test.tsx` (3), the menu test of `App.test.tsx` (eight items). **26 mutations, 25 caught** after two were closed with tests; the survivor is a guard the disabled buttons make unreachable.
Verification: full frontend 169 files / 3598 tests (the one older unhandled error of `ProjectDocuments` stays), `tsc` (also over the tests) and the whole `npm run build` PASS -- the second run of them after the lesson of release 2 found three type errors in my new tests (`Array.at`, a Node module without typings, a missing menu id), fixed before the commit; real Chromium with a fake Telegram at 320 / 390 / 412 px PL + RU: 18 layout checks clean, all nine probes ran (real WebCrypto, PBKDF2 and Argon2 in the browser: about 100 ms for 600000 PBKDF2 rounds and 400 ms for Argon2 64 MiB t3 on the build machine, the phone will differ). **Package:** `docs/CLIENT_ENCRYPTION_EN1_RUNBOOK_RU.md` (what the page is, the steps on the phone, how the result is read, the rollback) and `docs/CLIENT_ENCRYPTION_EN1_DEPLOY_RU.sh` (frontend only: G0 allows exactly one new dependency line `hash-wasm` 4.12.0 and at most 12 added lines in the lock file, nothing of the backend, Docker, compose or Caddy; gate B `ВЫКЛАДКА ДА`; G2 the markers of the page and the Argon2 chunk are served; G3 the backend container is the same one, healthy, the database on `0061`, the data the same; G4 Telegram button); dry run on stubs over a real git: 1 full pass and 19 refusals. Not deployed. **What it is for:** the report of the owner's phone decides the design of V2 (where the key of the owner is kept, whether biometrics are used, the parameters of the key derivation, what survives a reinstall); it does not block V1 (EN-2a).

## Permanent Product Rule: Mobile-First UI

**Canonical UI target is MOBILE FIRST** — Plan & Estimate is a Telegram Mini App intended primarily for on-site use from a smartphone. The frontend remains a web application because Telegram Mini Apps run inside Telegram WebView; there is **no separate desktop-oriented UI**. This rule is permanent and binds every future frontend execution sub-stage. Also codified in `CLAUDE.md`.

- **Primary working viewport**: 320–480 px width.
- **Primary manual acceptance viewports**: 390 px, 412 px.
- Localhost desktop browser usage is primarily a development and debugging environment.

1. Mobile layout is authoritative.
2. New UI must be designed first for approximately 390–412 px.
3. Every primary action must remain usable at 320 px minimum width unless a component has an explicitly documented exception.
4. No horizontal page scrolling.
5. Text, badges, and labels must wrap safely.
6. Long names must never collide with action buttons.
7. Prefer vertical stacking over squeezing controls horizontally.
8. Primary actions should normally use full available width where appropriate.
9. Touch targets should be approximately >=44 px for important interactive controls.
10. Avoid tiny icon-only controls for important actions unless their meaning is unambiguous.
11. Forms must use mobile-appropriate input behavior: `inputMode="decimal"` for decimal measurements, `inputMode="numeric"` where appropriate, and correct textarea/select/button sizing.
12. Telegram WebView navigation is authoritative: Telegram BackButton, application breadcrumbs/back hierarchy, and no desktop-only navigation dependency.
13. Do NOT spend development effort creating desktop-specific layouts unless explicitly requested by the project owner.
14. Responsive desktop behavior may remain functional, but desktop visual optimization is NOT an acceptance criterion.
15. Avoid adding `sm:`/`md:`/`lg:` layout changes merely to make the desktop version prettier when they complicate the mobile layout.
16. Every frontend execution sub-stage must include mobile regression verification.
17. For UI-heavy stages, acceptance must explicitly check: 390 px, 412 px, wrapping, overflow, touch targets, and long PL/RU translations.
18. Polish and Russian localization must be tested because Russian labels may be materially longer than Polish labels.

**Field-usage principle**: optimize workflows for a contractor standing at a construction site and using the phone with minimal taps — prefer short workflows, large controls, progressive disclosure, secondary actions hidden behind "Opcje" where appropriate, sensible defaults, reuse of previous/default dimensions where safe, and avoiding unnecessary screens and repeated data entry. This principle guides later Stage 5F/5G follow-up work, inspection workflows, photos, defect annotations, estimates, checklists, and reports. The rule is permanently documented; no screens are redesigned in this task.

**Stage 10 canonical decisions (preserved, still in force for all future stages that touch Estimate/PriceBook data):**
- Estimate is snapshot-based: each version is a point-in-time generation from the current Work Plan, never silently synchronized with later Work Plan changes.
- Regeneration is always explicit — "Sprawdź zmiany" (preview, read-only) then an explicit confirm; nothing recalculates automatically.
- `unit_price: null` means unresolved / "Do ustalenia" ("Цена уточняется"), strictly distinct from an explicit `0.00`.
- A market/reference price shown in the Price Book never silently substitutes for the owner's own price.
- A FINAL Estimate is immutable; historical Estimate versions are preserved and remain readable (including their original provenance) after a new version is generated.
- Reveal (ościeże) geometry is computed and stored independently of WALL net/gross area and opening deductions — reveal totals never feed back into wall area math.
- `PriceUnit.LM` reveal work quantifies by reveal length (`QuantitySource.REVEAL_LENGTH`); `PriceUnit.M2` reveal work quantifies by reveal area (`QuantitySource.REVEAL_AREA`).
- Work planning exists at two independent levels: per-Surface (`SurfaceWorkPlan`) and per-Opening/reveal (`OpeningRevealPlannedWork`).
- An owner-created inline PriceItem (from either the Surface Work Plan picker or the Reveal picker) is a normal, fully-editable PriceBook entity — not a special estimate-only record.

**Non-blocking backlog (preserved, none promoted into Stage 11):**
- **ARCHIVED RECORD HARD DELETE — DEFERRED.** Current behavior: archive/restore remains the only supported lifecycle for Client/Project/Room/Surface/Opening/Work Plan/Estimate-adjacent records; nothing is ever hard-deleted today. Future hard-delete work must first define an explicit dependency/safety matrix across `Client → Project → Room → Surface → Opening → Work Plans → Estimate provenance/history`, and must never silently destroy a historical Estimate snapshot, its provenance, or any other dependent record. This is **not** a Stage 10 blocker and is **not** assigned to Stage 11 — the canonical roadmap does not require it there.
- Proactive (pre-attempt) unresolved-price counter on the Estimate view (currently only a reactive, localized, owner-accepted finalize-rejection count exists).
- Scope subtotal footer (Robocizna/Materiały/Mieszane/Razem) on the Estimate view.
- Seeded-row compact Price Book price editor re-null toggle (parity with the full `PriceItemForm`'s "Cena do ustalenia" checkbox).
- Stage 5G compact Surface Card Actions polish, if still recorded elsewhere as outstanding.

Archive/restore is soft and explicit (no hard delete); a `CoefficientGroup` list/detail read model eager-loads its `options` in one extra query (no N+1), with archived options filtered at the API/schema layer rather than by mutating the ORM's `cascade="all, delete-orphan"` relationship collection (which would have marked filtered-out rows for deletion on the next flush — caught during implementation, not shipped). Two real async-session bugs were found and fixed during implementation, both instances of a pattern this codebase had already hit once before (`EstimateService.generate_estimate`'s own documented "avoid lazy-loading a relationship on a freshly-flushed object" precedent): (1) `selectinload` does not refresh an already-populated relationship collection on an identity-mapped object across separate `execute()` calls in the same session — fixed by adding `execution_options(populate_existing=True)` to every eager-loading query; (2) a freshly created/flushed object's untouched collection relationship can require a genuine (and, in an async session, disallowed) lazy load on first access post-commit — fixed by never touching `.options` on a bare service-returned object at the API layer, always re-fetching with eager loading first (mirroring the pattern already used for update/archive/restore). When the occurrence itself no longer exists (its WorkPlan/Reveal was edited since generation, so the old occurrence id is genuinely gone — not an error), reset honestly falls back to a bare `PriceItem.price` reload with `coefficient_snapshot=None` (not a fabricated `[]`) rather than guessing a selection it cannot determine — documented and tested explicitly. ### Client data encryption, EN-1: the measured results of the phone and the sharper probe (2026-10-18; branch `backlog-client-encryption`; not a roadmap stage)

**EN-1 deployed by the owner (version f2e1937, all gates PASS, backend and database untouched)**, the report of the phone (Telegram Android 13.0.2, Bot API 9.6, Android 16): WebCrypto AES-GCM ok; PBKDF2 100k = 37 ms, 300k = 52 ms, 600k = 105 ms; Argon2id 19 MiB t2 = 82 ms, 64 MiB t3 = 323 ms; CloudStorage ok, a value of 1024 and 4096 characters accepted, 4097 refused (`DATA_TOO_LONG`); SecureStorage and DeviceStorage write and read the value back (`canRestore=null` on SecureStorage) but **a read after the removal still answers a value (`after_remove=STILL_THERE`) -- unexplained**; biometrics **not available** on this phone (`available=false`, both taps answer `WebAppBiometricManagerBiometricsNotAvailable`); the three markers were written and read back within one session (the reinstall / new-phone test is still to do).
**Conclusion for V2:** the KDF is not a bottleneck (Argon2id 64 MiB t3 in 0.3 s); the wrapped owner key with its salt fits in CloudStorage (<= 4096 characters); biometrics cannot be a requirement; whether SecureStorage / DeviceStorage forget a removed value is to be settled.
**Probe refined (this commit):** after the removal the probe now prints the raw answer (`after_raw=` as JSON, so `null`, `""` and the string `"null"` are told apart), `after_can_restore=` and, when Telegram offers it, the result of `restoreItem`. Tests: `security/probe.test.ts` 40 (two new), the page and App tests unchanged; tsc and the whole `npm run build` pass. Not pushed, not deployed (needs the owner's "push" and the frontend deploy script).
**Deferred:** the reinstall / new-phone marker test; EN-2a (V1 base) waits for the owner's explicit "da".
**Second phone (Telegram-Android 13.0.1, older probe, report of 2026-10-18T08:54Z):** the same picture -- Bot API 9.6, WebCrypto, CloudStorage 4096 accepted / 4097 refused, biometrics `BiometricsNotAvailable`, SecureStorage and DeviceStorage again `after_remove=STILL_THERE` (so it is systematic, not a fluke of one build); PBKDF2 600k = 225 ms, Argon2id 64 MiB t3 = 1126 ms (the lower bound of the phones seen). That report holds only the `*.clear` lines of the markers (no `*.read`), so the reinstall test is still open.
**EN-1b deployment script (frontend only, no dependency change):** `docs/CLIENT_ENCRYPTION_EN1B_DEPLOY_RU.sh` -- like the EN-1 script, but G0 requires that `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are NOT changed, the tag is `pre-en1b`, G2 also looks for `after_raw=` and `after_can_restore=` in the served bundle; gate `ВЫКЛАДКА ДА`.
**EN-1b result (reports of phone A, Telegram-Android 13.0.2, and phone B, 13.0.1, 2026-10-18):** `after_raw="null"` -- with the quotes, i.e. the STRING `null`: **Telegram for Android answers a key that is not there with the string "null"**. So the removal works on SecureStorage and DeviceStorage; the `STILL_THERE` of the earlier reports was a mistake of the probe, not of the phones. Fixed: `isMissing()` takes `null`, `""` and `"null"` as "nothing stored" (probe, marker read); two tests. **For the V2 code:** the wrapper of the storages must treat the string `"null"` as a missing value. The markers: written on A in all three storages; on B (another phone) the reads give `secure.read: "null"` (= nothing), `device.read: "null"` (= nothing), `cloud.read: empty`, and the CloudStorage key count on B is 1 against 2 on A -- **the marker of A is not visible on B in any of the three storages**. The Secure/Device result is expected (they are local to a phone); the CloudStorage result is NOT expected if B is the same Telegram account (CloudStorage lives on Telegram's servers per user and bot): **to be clarified with the owner whether B is the same account**. Both phones: PBKDF2 600k 103 ms / 380 ms, Argon2id 64 MiB t3 310 ms / 710 ms (the earlier reading of 225 ms / 1126 ms was the same B phone under load); biometrics unavailable on both.

### Photo attachments
- Attachment context: Project / Room, `WALL` surface, `FLOOR`, `CEILING`.
- Capture methods: camera capture and gallery/file upload.
- Multiple photos per target.
- Description / notes and timestamps.
- Thumbnails.
- S3-compatible object-storage abstraction.
- Metadata stored separately from binary image data.

### Defect annotations
- User taps a point on the photo to place an annotation.
- Normalized `x` / `y` coordinates (resolution-independent).
- Multiple annotations per photo.
- Defect category, comment, severity, status.

Candidate defect categories may later include: crack, detachment, moisture, unevenness, mechanical damage, other. This candidate enum must **not** be frozen prematurely in implementation documentation.

### Future integration chain (documented intent, not implemented in Stage 5)

```
Photo / PhotoAnnotation
→ Inspection Checklist Finding
→ Risk Rules Engine
→ Recommended Work
→ Estimate
→ PDF / protective protocol
```

Clarifications:
- This dependency chain is forward integration intent recorded at Stage 5 closure. No element of it is implemented today.
- **Stage 6** (Inspection Checklist Engine) should design inspection findings so they can later reference photos/annotations, but Stage 6 must **not** implement photo storage.
- **Stage 7** (Risk Rules Engine) may later consume annotated defects as risk inputs.
- **Stage 11** (Inspection → recommended work → estimate) may later convert annotated/checklist findings into recommended work.
- **Stage 15** (Documents / PDF) may later embed selected photos/annotations into generated documents.
- **Stage 20** (Full MVP audit) should include the photo/defect workflow in its end-to-end audit scenario.

#### Execution Sub-Stage 5B: Openings, Deductions & Net Surface Area
- **Status**: Completed
- **Date**: 2026-09-10
- **Scope**:
  - Added first-class `Opening` entity attached strictly to `WALL` surfaces (`opening_type` in `DOOR`, `WINDOW`, `OTHER`).
  - High-precision dimensions in meters using `sa.Numeric(10, 3)` and Python `Decimal` (`width`, `height`, integer `quantity >= 1`).
  - Implemented pure domain opening area calculations in `app/domain/rules/room_geometry.py`:
    - `single_area = (width * height).quantize(Decimal("0.001"))`
    - `total_area = (width * height * quantity).quantize(Decimal("0.001"))`
    - Wall deduction area = sum of active opening deductions
    - Wall net area = `gross_area - deduction_area` (strictly non-negative; zero when deductions equal gross area)
    - Non-WALL surfaces (`FLOOR`, `CEILING`, `OTHER`) return `None` for deductions and net area.
  - Geometry integrity & over-deduction protection:
    - Prevented creating, updating, or restoring openings where deductions would exceed gross wall area (`DeductionExceedsGrossAreaError` -> HTTP 422).
    - Prevented shrinking wall surface dimensions smaller than existing active deductions (`DeductionExceedsGrossAreaError` -> HTTP 422).
    - Persisted state remains completely unchanged on rejected write operations.
  - Canonical acceptance room verified:
    - Room: $5.000 \times 4.000 \times 2.700\text{ m}$
    - Wall 1: $13.500\text{ m}^2$ gross, Door $0.900 \times 2.000\text{ m}$ ($1.800\text{ m}^2$), net $11.700\text{ m}^2$
    - Wall 2: $10.800\text{ m}^2$ gross, Window $1.500 \times 1.400\text{ m}$ ($2.100\text{ m}^2$), net $8.700\text{ m}^2$
    - Wall 3: $13.500\text{ m}^2$ gross, net $13.500\text{ m}^2$
    - Wall 4: $10.800\text{ m}^2$ gross, net $10.800\text{ m}^2$
    - Total gross wall area: $48.600\text{ m}^2$
    - Total deductions: $3.900\text{ m}^2$
    - Total net wall area: $44.700\text{ m}^2$ ($48.600 - 3.900 = 44.700\text{ m}^2$)
  - Room aggregation architecture:
    - Child-dependent totals calculated strictly in domain/service aggregation layer with zero N+1 queries.
    - `SurfaceService.list_surfaces` and `RoomService.list_rooms` use aggregated PostgreSQL subqueries outer-joined in single roundtrips.
    - Composite index `ix_openings_surface_archived(surface_id, is_archived)` for high query efficiency.
  - Archive/restore behavior:
    - Archiving opening excludes it from deductions and restores net wall area.
    - Restoring opening re-includes it in deductions, blocked if wall shrunk in between.
    - In multiple-opening setups, archiving one updates deductions accurately.
  - Transitive owner isolation across 4 levels (`Owner → Project → Room → Surface → Opening`):
    - Foreign/mismatched IDs return uniform 404 responses.
    - Unauthenticated requests return 401.

- **Status**: Completed (implementation verified)

  - **Non-destructive canonical wall generation**: `POST /api/projects/{project_id}/rooms/{room_id}/surfaces/generate` returns the 4 canonical rectangle walls from room `length × width × height` — Wall1/Wall3 = `length × height`, Wall2/Wall4 = `width × height`, positions 0–3, all `surface_type=WALL`. Domain layer uses language-neutral names; floor/ceiling are never auto-generated. Generation rules:
    - (A) room missing `length` / `width` / `height` → 422;
    - (B) no active WALLs → create exactly 4 canonical walls;
    - (C) active walls already equal the canonical set → idempotent no-op returning existing walls;
    - (D) any other configuration → 409 Conflict, modifying nothing.
  - **Wall-derived room totals**: pure-rule `calculate_wall_derived_totals` + `resolve_room_totals` aggregate measured WALL surfaces — `wall_count`, `perimeter = Σ widths`, `total_wall_area = Σ gross`, `total_deduction_area`, `net_wall_area` — with zero-N+1 queries in `RoomService`. Custom/irregular rooms report `floor_area = None` and `ceiling_area = None` (never fabricated); rectangles without walls keep formula geometry (`wall_count = 0`).
  - **Canonical acceptance values**: surface-derived totals exactly match the formula — perimeter `18.000`, gross `48.600`, door `0.900 × 2.000 → 1.800` + window `1.500 × 1.400 → 2.100` deductions → net `44.700`.
  - **Frontend wall input modes** (`PROSTOKĄT` / RECTANGLE vs `DOWOLNY KSZTAŁT` / CUSTOM — frontend state only, not persisted, no CAD/polygon editing):
    - Rectangle mode exposes `Wygeneruj 4 ściany` (generate action) when the room has dimensions; a generation conflict (409) is surfaced without hiding existing walls.
    - Custom mode provides sequential wall entry — the next empty row is UI state only and never persisted; submitting a row sends one real `WALL` with positional ordering, default height from `Room.height`, and an `Inna wysokość` override that sets `Surface.height`; no phantom/empty/zero-width requests.
    - Direct `+ Drzwi / + Okno / + Inny otwór` quick actions on every measured wall card open the opening form with the type pre-selected (`OpeningList.initialType`); no room-level openings.
  - **Room summary additions**: `wall_count` display; custom rooms render floor/ceiling as `—` (via `formatMetric`), with perimeter and totals derived from measured walls.

#### Execution Sub-Stage 5D.1B: Composite Floor & Ceiling Geometry
- **Status**: Completed

  - Pure domain rules in `app/domain/rules/room_geometry.py`:
    - `segment_area = width × height` quantized to `0.001 m²`
    - `calculate_plane_base_area(length, width)` → `L × W` for a RECTANGLE room, `None` for a CUSTOM room.
    - Per plane (base-aware): `base_area = L × W` (RECTANGLE) or `0` (CUSTOM); `additive_area = Σ active ADD`, `subtraction_area = Σ active SUBTRACT`, `net_area = base_area + additive − subtraction`.
    - Zero net allowed; negative net rejected (`NegativeNetAreaError` → HTTP 422 on create/update/restore) using the **same** base-aware effective total (a RECTANGLE subtraction may deduct from the room base); archived segments always excluded.
  - Room total resolution (`resolve_room_totals`):
    - A plane with active segments → effective `net_area` (base + adjustments).
    - A RECTANGLE plane with no segments → existing formula `L × W` base (never `0.000`).
    - A CUSTOM (no dims) plane with no segments → `None`.
    - FLOOR and CEILING resolved independently; a segments-only branch lets an irregular room measured purely as composite planes still yield calculations (never fabricates rectangular `L × W`).
  - `RoomService.list_rooms` aggregates active segments in a single grouped query per project (zero N+1, constant query count); `get_room` loads both planes in one query.
  - API `/api/projects/{project}/rooms/{room}/area-segments`: list (with `?plane=` filter, `?include_archived=`), create, get, patch, archive, restore. Pydantic v2 DTOs validate `Decimal gt=0`, `decimal_places=3`, `max_digits=10`; owner isolation intact (foreign → 404, unauthenticated → 401).

#### Execution Sub-Stage 5D.1B.2 (Hotfix): Rectangle Base-Area Semantics
- **Status**: Completed
- **Date**: 2026-09-11
- **Problem**: Rectangle plane totals were computed from active segments only, ignoring the room `L × W` base — a rectangle with zero segments showed `total = 0.000`, and a lone `SUBTRACT 0.700 × 0.800` was rejected as `0.000 − 0.560 < 0`. The frontend duplicated the segment-only calculation as its display source.
- **Calculation fix (backend authoritative)**:
  - `calculate_plane_base_area(length, width)` returns `L × W` for RECTANGLE, `None` for CUSTOM.
  - `calculate_plane_totals(segments, base_area=None)` computes `net = base_area + Σ ADD − Σ SUBTRACT`; the negative guard uses the same effective total. `PlaneAreaTotals` gains `base_area`.
  - `area_segment_service._assert_plane_net_non_negative` loads the room base, so create/update/restore of a SUBTRACT may deduct from the rectangle base.
  - `room_service._load_plane_segment_totals` / `list_rooms` fold the base into room `calculations.floor_area` / `ceiling_area`; removed the dead `_plane_totals_from_segments`.
  - `AreaSegmentListResponse` gains `planes: {FLOOR, CEILING} → {base_area, adjustment_area, net_area}` (adjustment = ADD − SUBTRACT).
  - **No DB migration** — pure calculation + response DTO; Alembic head remains `0010`.
- **UI fix**: `AreaSegmentList` renders the backend-provided per-plane summary (`Powierzchnia bazowa` / `Korekty` / `Razem`) instead of computing totals; a rectangle never shows `0.000` for a known base, and a CUSTOM room shows no base row and no fabricated total. Added `base_area` / `adjustments` locale keys (PL/RU).
- **Verified examples**: `3.700 × 3.300` → base `12.210`; SUBTRACT `0.700 × 0.800` → `11.650`; ADD `1.000 × 0.500` → `12.710`; SUBTRACT `4.000 × 4.000` (16 > 12.210) → 422; FLOOR adjustment leaves CEILING at `12.210`; archive/restore recalculates against base (`11.650 → 12.210 → 11.650`); CUSTOM unchanged (no base, no segments → `None`, segments → `ADD − SUBTRACT` only).

#### Execution Sub-Stage 6B: Inspection Checklist Engine — Backend
- **Status**: Completed

  - **Inspection engine** (`Inspection` / `InspectionAnswer` / `InspectionFinding`): room-scoped inspections under `/api/projects/{project_id}/rooms/{room_id}/inspections` with four valid targets — (A) a specific `WALL` surface, (B) `FLOOR` plane, (C) `CEILING` plane, (D) room-level (both `surface_id` and `plane` null); the only rejected combination is both set; non-WALL surface targets rejected 422; owner isolation uniform (foreign → 404, unauthenticated → 401).
  - **Typed answers** (`AnswerType` BOOLEAN / NUMBER / TEXT / SINGLE_CHOICE / MULTI_CHOICE) stored in exact typed columns (`value_bool`, `value_number` Numeric(10,3), `value_text` String(4096), `option_key`, `option_keys` JSON); replace-set PUT semantics (previous answers dropped, incoming set becomes whole state, atomic via DELETE+flush+INSERT); unknown question / wrong option / wrong value shape / duplicate question rejected 422; edits frozen once COMPLETED.
  - **Factual findings** (`InspectionFinding`): materialize ONLY from explicit `finding_key` on a question or option (BOOL true / NUMBER present / non-empty TEXT / selected SINGLE_CHOICE option / each selected keyed MULTI_CHOICE option); a positive NUMBER alone is never a generic finding; `value_snapshot` JSON captures the factual value at materialization.
  - **Finding lifecycle**: reconciliation identity `(question_id, finding_key)` — same source reuses a stable UUID (refreshed snapshot/source), two distinct questions sharing a finding_key stay distinct findings, disappeared sources become `is_active = False` with `resolved_at` set and are never physically deleted; `answer_id`/`question_id` use `ON DELETE SET NULL` for downstream `PhotoAnnotation.finding_id` compatibility (Stage 14).
  - **Quality-scale validation** (`assert_quality_scale_valid`): `GYPSUM_BOARD` → `Q1`–`Q4`; `CONCRETE` / `GYPSUM_PLASTER` / `CEMENT_LIME_PLASTER` → `S1`–`S4`; `PAINTED` / `OTHER` unrestricted (quality target optional); PSG aliases are not stored as separate DB values.
  - **State lifecycle**: `DRAFT → COMPLETED → reopen → DRAFT`; `completed_at` set/cleared; re-completion re-reconciles findings; archive/restore convention (soft `is_archived`, default listing excludes archived).
  - **Initial templates**: 6 baseline templates (substrate-concrete, substrate-gypsum-plaster, substrate-cement-lime-plaster, substrate-gypsum-board with extra `drywall_joints` section, substrate-painted, substrate-other) covering general condition, cracking (CRACK), unevenness (UNEVENNESS), loose/dusty/oily substrate, delamination/blow-holes/efflorescence/mold, high moisture, weak adhesion, and notes.

#### Execution Sub-Stage 7B: Risk Rules Engine — Backend (Completed)
- **Status**: Completed (owner-verified 2026-09-12)
- **Date**: 2026-09-12
- **Scope**:
  - **Versioned immutable rule catalog** (`RiskRule` / `RiskRuleCondition`): named `(code, version)` unique constraint, 15 initial deterministic rules (CRACK_RECURRENCE, BOARD_MOVEMENT_CRACK, MOISTURE_BLOCK_FINISHING, WEAK_ADHESION_PREP, LOOSE_SUBSTRATE_REMOVAL, DUSTY_SUBSTRATE_PRIME, OILY_SUBSTRATE_DEGREASE, MOLD_TREATMENT_BEFORE_FINISH, DELAMINATION_REPAIR, UNEVENNESS_PREP_INCREASED, JOINT_TAPE_MISSING_REWORK, FASTENER_CORROSION_FIX, JOINT_GAP_FILLING, EFFLORESCENCE_CAUSE_CHECK, BLOW_HOLES_FILLING) with severity, `blocks_finishing`, `warranty_exclusion_candidate`, optional substrate restriction, and 5 i18n keys each; idempotent DB-reset-safe bootstrap (`RiskService._ensure_bootstrapped`, `asyncio.Lock`-serialized); no CRUD API (catalog is reference data).
  - **8 condition operators** (all-AND within a rule): `FINDING_PRESENT`, `FINDING_ABSENT`, `NUMBER_AT_LEAST`, `NUMBER_AT_MOST`, `SUBSTRATE_IN`, `SUBSTRATE_NOT_IN`, `TARGET_IN`, `QUALITY_IN`; numeric thresholds (e.g. UNEVENNESS ≥ 3 mm, JOINT_GAP ≥ 2 mm) are **initial domain defaults** stored in condition `value_json`, tunable as reference data; malformed/missing numeric snapshots fail safely (rule does not fire).
  - **Deterministic evaluation** (`domain/rules/risk_rules.py`): pure engine over inspection substrate/quality/target + active findings; overlapping rules may all fire (no hidden suppression); source signature = SHA-256 over sorted source finding UUIDs (order-independent, part of the stable risk identity).
  - **Risk materialization** (`Risk` / `RiskFinding`): room- and inspection-scoped rows under `/api/projects/{project_id}/rooms/{room_id}/risks`; identity `(inspection_id, rule_code, source_signature)` enforced by a unique constraint — identical inspection state always yields the same row with a stable UUID; risk rows carry `risk_code`/`rule_code`/`rule_version`, severity, 5 i18n key snapshots, `blocks_finishing`, `warranty_exclusion_candidate`, `is_active`/`resolved_at`, and ordered `source_findings` links that snapshot finding key + value even if the source finding FK later goes NULL.
  - **Reconciliation on evaluate**: `POST .../risks/evaluate` is idempotent; a reused identity keeps its UUID and its original `rule_version`/text-key snapshot (version preservation), only refreshing activity state and source-finding links; previously confirmed risks absent from the new evaluation become `is_active = False` with `resolved_at` set and are never deleted; evaluation rejected 409 unless the inspection is COMPLETED (no DB writes on rejection).
  - **API contract**: `GET .../risks` (filters: `inspection_id`, `surface_id`, `plane`, `status=active|resolved|all`), `GET .../risks/{risk_id}` (detail with source findings), `POST .../risks/evaluate` (idempotent, returns active risks with source findings); owner isolation uniform (foreign → 404, unauthenticated → 401); grouped source-finding loading (no N+1 on batch evaluate).
- **Database**:
  - Migration: `backend/alembic/versions/0012_create_risk_engine.py` (parent `0011_create_inspection_engine`; sole Alembic head).
  - Tables created: `risk_rules`, `risk_rule_conditions`, `risks`, `risk_findings`; enums `riskseverity`, `riskconditionoperator`; `risk_rules.substrate` reuses the `substrate` type owned by migration 0011 (`create_type=False`); unique `(code, version)` on rules, unique `(inspection_id, rule_code, source_signature)` on risks, unique `(risk_id, finding_id)` on links.
  - Reversibility: `downgrade -1` then `upgrade head` verified on real PostgreSQL; downgrade drops tables child-first + enum types and leaves `substrate` to 0011; all four tables restored after the cycle.

A future project-wide phrase overview may be added later and is **not** part of Stage 8 MVP.
- **8A.1 correction 2 — no second rule engine**: the Stage 8 selection space is **exact-key matching** over already-evaluated, already-materialized facts — active Risk codes, active `InspectionFinding` keys, `substrate`, `quality_target` — not a condition graph. The proposed `CommunicationRule` + `CommunicationRuleCondition` + operator evaluator (8A draft) is **removed**. Alternatives evaluated:
  - **A — Risk → phrase directly through the existing `RiskRule.communication_key`**: correct base behavior for risk-derived phrases and **used as the seed key**, but alone cannot express Stage 8's categories (8 semantic categories), finding-only phrases (no Risk), quality-level phrases, or the "why" corridor → insufficient alone.
  - **B — Risk → versioned `CommunicationPhrase` mapping, without another condition engine** (chosen): a single versioned reference-data table whose rows are selected by direct trigger-key equality (risk_code / finding_key / substrate / quality_level), plus a thin per-inspection materialized reference. Deterministic by construction, trivially auditable, versioned/historically stable, extensible by adding rows — no operators, no thresholds, no conjunctions, no parallel evaluation path that could diverge from Stage 7.
  - **C — independent `CommunicationRule` + conditions engine (rejected)**: duplicates Stage 7 machinery; a phrase trigger space needs no operator evaluator. Revisit only if a future stage demonstrates compound conditions — which would live in the canonical Stage 7 engine, not a new one.
  - **WHY NOT ANOTHER CONDITION ENGINE**: Stage 7 needs operators because a *risk* is a logical conjunction (multi-finding, `NUMBER_AT_LEAST` thresholds, substrate/target/quality membership). Stage 8 consumes facts **already derived by that engine** (an active Risk is itself the evaluated product) or raw keys (finding_key, substrate, quality_target). Selecting a phrase by exact key equality requires a lookup over versioned reference data, not a general evaluator; a second engine would recompute Stage 7 logic (unacceptable — no Stage 6/7 recomputation, traceability must read materialized state only) for zero behavioral gain.
- **8A.1 decision — Stage 7 `communication_key` role**: each `RiskRule`/materialized `Risk` snapshots `communication_key = risk.<slug>.communication` (one of five auto-derived i18n keys via `risk_service._rule_keys()`; 15 rules, full PL/RU parity; currently dormant in the Stage 7 UI which deliberately does not render it). Stage 8 **consumes, never duplicates** it: risk-derived phrase definitions declare a `seed_key = risk.<slug>.communication` and render the existing Stage 7 PL/RU phrase text (weighted by category/priority; severity/flag emphasis is rendered from Risk fields, not new text). The "why" corridor uses the risk's own snapshotted `explanation/consequence` keys + source `RiskFinding`/`InspectionFinding` value snapshots — never recomputing Stage 6/7 logic. New Stage 8 text exists only in a dedicated `communication.*` locale namespace; `risk.*` keys are **never modified**.
- **8A.1 finding-only strategy**: a simple deterministic mapping `finding_key (+ optional substrate) (+ optional quality_target) → phrase`, implemented as `communication_phrases` rows with finding_key/substrate/quality_level trigger columns; selection = best-match (specificity-descending exact-key lookup). No condition evaluator.
- **8A.1 quality strategy**: explicit deterministic reference data `substrate + quality_target → phrase` (category `QUALITY_EXPECTATION` / `GENERAL`), rows keyed by substrate + quality_level. Where the substrate's scale is not applicable (e.g., `PAINTED`/`OTHER`), the catalog provides `GENERAL` wording. No second engine; a generic evaluator is not justified by two-key equality.
- **8A.1 materialization strategy (compare / decision)**: a full transactional per-phrase recommendation row set with source-link table and value snapshots (Risk-style, option 1) is **rejected as over-engineered** — trigger values already live in Stage 6/7 snapshots, and phrases are not long-lived status entities. Purely recomputed/read-only output (option 0) is **rejected** — a later catalog release would silently change previously shown phrases, violating historical reproducibility. **Decision — hybrid minimal (option 2)**: (a) immutable, versioned **phrase definitions** (`communication_phrases`) deliver determinism, versioning, and historical stability of released content; (b) a **thin per-inspection application record** (`communication_applications`) freezes exactly which (phrase_code, phrase_version) applied at evaluation time, snapshotting the rendering keys, so previously shown phrases never drift. Persisted: phrase definitions + per-inspection applied references + key/version snapshots. **Not persisted**: no value snapshots (already in Stage 6/7), no source-link join table (trigger keys declared on the phrase row; the actual values are read from the already-persisted Risk/Finding rows for the "why" disclosure), no status-family lifecycle beyond `is_active`/`resolved_at` for re-evaluation reconciliation.
- **8A.1 minimal API (inspection-contextual — chosen)**: routes are nested under the inspection, mirroring the existing inspection sub-resource family (`/answers`, `/findings`, `/complete`) and the canonical mobile flow, with the inspection id in the path (no body ambiguity, one substrate/quality/target context per request):
  - `GET /api/projects/{project_id}/rooms/{room_id}/inspections/{inspection_id}/communications?status=active|all` — materialized communication phrases for one COMPLETED inspection.
  - `POST /api/projects/{project_id}/rooms/{room_id}/inspections/{inspection_id}/communications/evaluate` — idempotent evaluation/reconciliation (409 unless COMPLETED), returns applied phrases + trigger keys.
  - `GET /api/projects/{project_id}/rooms/{room_id}/inspections/{inspection_id}/communications/{communication_id}` — single application detail incl. source context for the "why" disclosure (**traceability without frontend/backend Stage 6/7 recomputation**).
  - Rationale vs. room-level family (`/communications?inspection_id=`): inspection-contextual matches the MVP intent (phrases only exist inside a completed-inspection results workflow), removes the `inspection_id` ambiguity/optionality from the query, and keeps POST /evaluate naturally per-inspection; a future project-wide overview adds its own route later (not Stage 8 MVP). No generic CRUD.
- **8A.1 minimal 0013 migration plan (propose only — NOT created; 8B will implement)**: exactly **two** tables (no conditions table, no source-link table, no value snapshots):
  - `communication_phrases` — id UUID pk; code String(120); version Integer; active Boolean default true; category Enum(`communicationcategory`); priority Integer; trigger columns all nullable + indexed: `risk_code String(120)`, `finding_key String(120)`, `substrate Enum(substrate)`, `quality_level Enum(qualitylevel)`; `phrase_key String(255)`; `why_key String(255)`; `seed_key String(255)` nullable (Stage 7 reuse); created_at/updated_at. Unique `(code, version)`; index `(active, category)`.
  - `communication_applications` — id UUID pk; inspection_id FK→inspections.id ON DELETE CASCADE; `phrase_code String(120)`; `phrase_version Integer`; category; priority; `phrase_key`/`why_key`/`seed_key` snapshots; `is_active Boolean`; `resolved_at timestamptz`; position; created_at/updated_at. Unique `(inspection_id, phrase_code, phrase_version)`; index `(inspection_id, is_active)`.
  - Reversible upgrade/downgrade; single Alembic head `0013_create_communication_engine`; reference data materialized by service bootstrap (`build_baseline_communication_phrases`), never Alembic-seeded (ChecklistTemplate/RiskRule pattern).

Phrase cards are short and immediately usable on site: primary phrase visible immediately; category chip; placeholder copy action; "Why?" / source context progressively disclosed (risk explanation/consequence or finding values via the permanent two-decimal policy). No desktop-specific layouts.

Sprawdź odpowiedzi.") instead of "Request failed (422)".
